title.zh: 卷410 列傳一百九十七 彭玉麟 杨岳斌 王明山 孙昌凯 杨明海 谢濬畬
title.en: Volume 410 Biographies 197: Peng Yulin, Yang Yuebin, Wang Mingshan, Sun Changkai, Yang Minghai, Xie Junshe
title.raw: 卷410 列傳一百九十七 彭玉麟 杨岳斌 王明山 孙昌凯 杨明海 谢濬畬

sentences.zh: =彭玉麟=彭玉麟，字雪琴，湖南衡陽人。

translations.literal: Biography of Peng Yulin. Peng Yulin, styled Xueqin, was a native of Hengyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Peng Yulin. Peng Yulin, courtesy name Xueqin, came from Hengyang in Hunan Province.

sentences.zh: 父鳴九，官安徽合肥梁園巡檢。

translations.literal: His father Mingjiu served as patrol inspector of Liangyuan in Hefei, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Peng Mingjiu held the post of patrol inspector at Liangyuan in Hefei, Anhui.

sentences.zh: 玉麟年十六，父卒，族人奪其田產，避居郡城，為協標書識以養母。

translations.literal: When Yulin was sixteen, his father died; clansmen seized his family's fields and property, so he moved to the prefectural city for refuge and worked as a clerk in the garrison headquarters to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, after his father's death, relatives seized the family lands; Yulin fled to the prefectural seat and took work as a clerk in the local militia headquarters to provide for his mother.

sentences.zh: 知府高人鑑見其文，奇之，招入署讀書，為附生。

translations.literal: Prefect Gao Renjian read his compositions, found them remarkable, summoned him to study in the yamen, and enrolled him as a government student.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Gao Renjian, impressed by his writing, brought him into the office to study and had him enrolled as a government-sponsored student.

sentences.zh: 新寧匪亂，從協標剿捕。

translations.literal: When rebels rose in Xinning, he joined the garrison in campaigns to suppress and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebel uprising in Xinning, he served with the local garrison in suppression operations.

sentences.zh: 敘功，大吏誤以為武生，拔補臨武營外委，不就。

translations.literal: When merits were recorded, a high official mistakenly took him for a military licentiate and selected him for appointment as an outside officer in the Linwu battalion, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were tallied, a provincial superior wrongly identified him as a military licentiate and offered him an outside appointment in the Linwu battalion, which he declined.

sentences.zh: 至耒陽，佐當商理事。

translations.literal: He went to Leiyang and assisted in managing commercial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Leiyang, where he helped administer local commerce.

sentences.zh: 粵匪至，罄所有資助縣令募勇籌防。

translations.literal: When Guangdong rebels arrived, he expended all he possessed to assist the magistrate in recruiting braves and preparing defenses.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel forces from Guangdong appeared, he gave everything he had to help the county magistrate raise militia and organize defenses.

sentences.zh: 賊知有備，不來攻，城獲全。

translations.literal: The rebels, knowing preparations had been made, did not come to attack, and the city was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the city was prepared, the rebels did not attack, and the walled town was spared.

sentences.zh: 玉麟不原敘功，但乞償所假錢，以是知名。

translations.literal: Yulin did not seek credit for merit, but only asked reimbursement for the money he had borrowed, and by this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin refused official recognition for his service and asked only to be repaid what he had borrowed, and on this account his name became known.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，曾國籓治水師，成十營，闢領一營。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, Zeng Guofan organized the navy, formed ten battalions, and established one battalion under his own command.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853, Zeng Guofan built the river fleet into ten battalions and personally commanded one of them.

sentences.zh: 其九營多武員，白事悉倚玉麟，隱主全軍，草創規制多所贊畫。

translations.literal: The other nine battalions were mostly led by military officers; for all reporting they relied entirely on Yulin, who secretly directed the whole force and contributed much to the initial regulations and plans.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the other nine battalions were commanded by career officers who reported chiefly to Yulin; though he held no formal title over the fleet, he quietly directed it and drew up many of its founding rules.

sentences.zh: 四年，初出師規岳州，不利，退長沙。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on the first campaign against Yuezhou, they met with no success and withdrew to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 their first advance on Yuezhou failed, and the fleet fell back to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 玉麟偕楊岳斌援湘潭，會塔齊布陸師夾攻，賊舟連檣十里，分三隊合擊，同時縱火焚其輜重皆盡。

translations.literal: Yulin joined Yang Yuebin in relieving Xiangtan; together with Ta Qibu's land forces they attacked from both sides; rebel vessels stretched in a line ten li long; they divided into three squads for a combined assault and at the same time set fire, burning all the rebel baggage to ashes.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin and Yang Yuebin went to relieve Xiangtan, coordinating with Ta Qibu's infantry in a pincer attack; rebel boats lined the river for ten li, and three squadrons struck together and burned the enemy stores completely.

sentences.zh: 賊棄城走，复湘潭，敘功以知縣選用。

translations.literal: The rebels abandoned the city and fled; Xiangtan was recovered, and for recorded merit he was nominated for appointment as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled the city; Xiangtan was retaken, and Yulin's merits were recorded with nomination for a county magistracy.

sentences.zh: 六月，再進岳州，賊據南津以拒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they advanced again on Yuezhou; the rebels held Nanjin to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In June the fleet advanced on Yuezhou again, but the rebels held Nanjin and blocked the way.

sentences.zh: 玉麟伏君山，岳斌伏雷公湖，遣小舟挑戰，賊舟爭出，兩翼鈔之，毀百餘艘，賊來，迭敗之。

translations.literal: Yulin lay in ambush at Junshan and Yuebin at Leigong Lake; they sent small boats to provoke battle; rebel vessels rushed out and were flanked on both wings and destroyed, more than a hundred in all; when the rebels came again, they were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin hid at Junshan while Yuebin concealed his boats at Leigong Lake; small craft drew the rebel fleet out, whereupon wing squadrons enveloped and destroyed more than a hundred vessels, beating back every counterattack.

sentences.zh: 進攻擂鼓台，賊舟多於官軍十倍。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Leigutai, rebel vessels outnumbered the government fleet ten to one.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Leigutai, rebel boats outnumbered the imperial navy tenfold.

sentences.zh: 玉麟偕岳斌各乘舢板冒砲煙衝入，燒其坐船，賊還救，陣亂，大破之，玉麟傷指，血染襟袖，軍中推二人勇略為冠。

translations.literal: Yulin and Yuebin each boarded sampans and charged through cannon smoke, burning the rebel command boat; the rebels turned back to rescue and their formation broke; they were routed; Yulin wounded a finger and blood stained his collar and sleeves; the army acclaimed the two as foremost in courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin and Yuebin each took a sampan through the barrage, set fire to the enemy flagship, and threw the rebel line into confusion; Yulin's finger was wounded and blood soaked his sleeves, and the fleet hailed the pair as the bravest commanders in the service.

sentences.zh: 既而總兵陳輝龍至，率新軍出戰，軍容甚盛，玉麟偕諸營從觀戰，拕罟膠淺，為賊所乘，急往救，水急風利，陷賊屯中，遂大敗。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Major General Chen Huilong arrived, leading newly raised troops into battle with imposing array; Yulin and the other battalions followed to observe; their towed nets ran aground in shallow water and the rebels seized the chance; he rushed to the rescue; the current was swift and the wind favorable, and they were trapped in the rebel encampment and suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Major General Chen Huilong arrived with fresh troops and marched out in grand array, Yulin and the other battalions watched from the river; tow-nets snagged in the shallows, the rebels exploited the mishap, and a rescue attempt swept Yulin's boats into the enemy anchorage, ending in disaster.

sentences.zh: 輝龍等戰歿，玉麟單舸退，自是水師專任彭、楊。

translations.literal: Huilong and others died in battle; Yulin retreated alone in a single boat; from then on the navy was entrusted solely to Peng and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huilong and several officers were killed; Yulin escaped in a lone boat, and thereafter the river fleet depended entirely on Peng Yulin and Yang Yuebin.

sentences.zh: 時陸軍累捷，賊退走，水師並進。

translations.literal: At that time the land army won repeated victories and the rebels retreated; the navy advanced together.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the land forces kept winning, the rebels fell back, and the fleet pushed forward in concert.

sentences.zh: 八月，屯沌口，規武昌。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they encamped at Dunkou and planned an advance on Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In August the fleet anchored at Dunkou and prepared to move on Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 玉麟與諸軍議，請渡江先破城外賊屯。

translations.literal: Yulin consulted with the other armies and requested to cross the river first and destroy the rebel encampments outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin urged the allied commanders to cross the Yangtze first and smash the rebel camps outside Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 賊自塘角至青山，緣岸列砲，丸發如雨。

translations.literal: From Tangjiao to Qingshan the rebels lined cannon along the shore, and shot fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel batteries stretched from Tangjiao to Qingshan, and round shot poured down like rain.

sentences.zh: 將士皆露立舢板，棹船徐進，無一俯側避砲者。

translations.literal: Officers and men all stood exposed on their sampans, rowing slowly forward, and not one bent or dodged to avoid the cannon.
translations.idiomatic: Sailors stood upright on open sampans and rowed steadily forward without a man ducking or flinching from the guns.

sentences.zh: 賊望見奪氣，沿江賊屯盡潰，悉燒屯壘及其舟。

translations.literal: The rebels, seeing this, lost heart; rebel encampments along the river all collapsed; all their stockades and boats were burned.
translations.idiomatic: The sight broke rebel morale; riverside camps collapsed one after another, and every stockade and boat was put to the torch.

sentences.zh: 武昌、漢陽同日皆复，論功擢同知。

translations.literal: Wuchang and Hanyang were recovered on the same day; for merit he was promoted to subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang and Hanyang fell on the same day, and Yulin was promoted to subprefect for his part in the victory.

sentences.zh: 群賊麕聚田家鎮，夾江為五屯，依半壁山，連舟斷江，纜以鐵索，布竹木為大筏，施大砲。

translations.literal: Massed rebels gathered at Tianjiazhen, forming five encampments on both banks of the river, leaning on Banbishan; they linked boats to block the river, moored with iron chains, laid out bamboo and timber as great rafts, and mounted heavy cannon.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel forces massed at Tianjiazhen in five riverside camps backed by Banbishan, chaining boats across the Yangtze with iron cables, building huge rafts of bamboo and timber, and mounting heavy guns.

sentences.zh: 筏外護以舟，後列輜重，望之如大城。

translations.literal: Outside the rafts boats served as a screen; behind them baggage was arrayed; viewed from afar it looked like a great city.
translations.idiomatic: Smaller craft shielded the rafts, supply trains lined up behind them, and from a distance the whole formation looked like a walled city.

sentences.zh: 武昌既克，水師欲下攻，而為蘄州江岸賊所撓。

translations.literal: Once Wuchang had been taken, the navy wished to push downstream, but was harassed by rebels on the Qizhou riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuchang fell the fleet meant to drive downstream, but rebels along the Qizhou shore repeatedly interfered.

sentences.zh: 玉麟掠江直下，十月，進逼田家鎮。

translations.literal: Yulin swept down the river; in the tenth month he pressed close to Tianjiazhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin raced downriver and by October had closed on Tianjiazhen.

sentences.zh: 與楊岳斌議分四隊，約陸師同時合擊。

translations.literal: He consulted with Yang Yuebin on dividing into four squads and arranged with the land army for a simultaneous combined attack.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yang Yuebin divided the fleet into four squadrons and timed a joint assault with the land forces.

sentences.zh: 頭隊皆小船，具爐備椎斧，融炭以待。

translations.literal: The vanguard were all small boats, equipped with furnaces and prepared with mauls and axes, melting charcoal in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: The lead squadron used small boats fitted with forges, mauls, and axes, with charcoal ready to melt the iron chains.

sentences.zh: 順流急趨，至筏下，斷鎖纜得隙，擠而過，後者從之。

translations.literal: Rushing downstream they reached the rafts, severed the chains and cables to gain an opening, squeezed through, and those behind followed.
translations.idiomatic: Racing downstream they reached the barrier, cut the chains, forced a gap, and slipped through while the rest of the squadron followed.

sentences.zh: 大呼曰：「鐵鎖開矣！」

translations.literal: He shouted loudly: "The iron chains are open!"
translations.idiomatic: He shouted at the top of his voice: "The chains are broken!"

sentences.zh: 賊驚噪，爭走相踐墮水。

translations.literal: The rebels panicked and clamored, scrambling to flee and trampling one another into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Panic swept the rebel ranks; men stampeded, trampling one another into the river.

sentences.zh: 玉麟率二隊順流而下，岳斌率三隊乘風而上，風起火烈，燒毀賊舟四千餘艘，奪獲五百餘艘。

translations.literal: Yulin led the second squadron downstream and Yuebin led the third upstream; wind rose and fire blazed; more than four thousand rebel boats were burned and destroyed and more than five hundred captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin's second squadron drove downstream while Yuebin's third pushed upstream; wind fanned the flames, destroying more than four thousand rebel boats and capturing over five hundred.

sentences.zh: 玉麟慮軍士互爭，盡焚之。

translations.literal: Yulin, fearing that soldiers would quarrel over spoils, burned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing quarrels over booty, Yulin ordered every captured vessel burned.

sentences.zh: 捷入，以知府記名。

translations.literal: When the victory was reported, he was registered for appointment as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: News of the victory reached the throne, and he was marked for appointment as prefect.

sentences.zh: 詔採其戰法頒下江南北諸水軍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his battle methods collected and issued to river fleets north and south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered his tactics copied and distributed to every Yangtze fleet north and south.

sentences.zh: 遂會諸軍進攻九江，連破賊於小池口、湖口。

translations.literal: Then the allied armies advanced on Jiujiang and repeatedly defeated the rebels at Xiao-chikou and Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: The combined forces then attacked Jiujiang, winning repeated victories at Xiao-chikou and Hukou.

sentences.zh: 賊於九江夜襲水師大營，帥舟被燔，曾國籓移駐陸軍。

translations.literal: At Jiujiang the rebels raided the navy's main camp by night; the commander's boat was burned, and Zeng Guofan moved his headquarters to the land army.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels night-assaulted the fleet's Jiujiang camp and burned the commander's vessel, forcing Zeng Guofan to shift his headquarters ashore.

sentences.zh: 玉麟部將蕭捷三追賊入鄱陽湖，賊斷湖口。

translations.literal: Yulin's subordinate Xiao Jiesan pursued rebels into Poyang Lake, and the rebels blocked Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate Xiao Jiesan chased rebels into Poyang Lake, where they sealed off Hukou.

sentences.zh: 玉麟往救不利，乃還新堤籌濟師。

translations.literal: Yulin went to the rescue but met with no success and returned to Xindi to prepare supplies for the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin's relief attempt failed, and he withdrew to Xindi to rebuild supplies for the fleet.

sentences.zh: 五年，武、漢复陷，玉麟更募士造船，立新軍，合三千人，與楊岳斌分統之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Wuchang and Hankou fell again; Yulin recruited men anew, built boats, established a new force of three thousand men, and divided command with Yang Yuebin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 Wuchang and Hankou were lost again; Yulin raised a new three-thousand-man fleet and shared command with Yang Yuebin.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼約同攻漢口，玉麟自金口進，敗賊鮎魚套；

translations.literal: Hu Linyi arranged a joint attack on Hankou; Yulin advanced from Jinkou and defeated the rebels at Nianyutao;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi planned a joint assault on Hankou; Yulin moved up from Jinkou and routed the rebels at Nianyutao;

sentences.zh: 北岸陸軍為賊所挫，玉麟率眾登岸截擊，破之，攻塘角，焚賊船二百餘：授浙江金華知府。

translations.literal: The land army on the north bank was checked by the rebels; Yulin led his men ashore to intercept and attack, broke them, assaulted Tangjiao, and burned more than two hundred rebel boats: he was appointed prefect of Jinhua in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel fire stalled the northern shore infantry, Yulin landed, cut them off, stormed Tangjiao, and burned more than two hundred boats; he was appointed prefect of Jinhua in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 七月，自沌口進拔蔡店，及南北兩岸石城。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he advanced from Dunkou and took Caidian and the stone forts on both north and south banks.
translations.idiomatic: In July he advanced from Dunkou, capturing Caidian and the stone forts on both banks.

sentences.zh: 五顯廟者，賊堅巢也。

translations.literal: Wuxianmiao was a rebel stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxianmiao was a rebel bastion.

sentences.zh: 阻湖而屯，玉麟攻之不下，曰：「已入虎穴，非血戰不能成功。」

translations.literal: Blocked by the lake in their encampment, Yulin could not take it and said: "Having entered the tiger's den, success cannot be won without bloody fighting."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held a lake-side camp Yulin could not crack; he declared, "We are already in the tiger's den—only a bloody fight will finish this."

sentences.zh: 張兩翼急槳而進，衝賊船尾，摧其卡，奪其船。

translations.literal: He spread both wings and rowed hard forward, striking the sterns of rebel boats, destroying their barriers, and seizing their vessels.
translations.idiomatic: He sent wings wide, rowed hard into the rebel line, smashed their barriers from the stern, and seized their boats.

sentences.zh: 复督隊徑越賊船，循兩岸包鈔。

translations.literal: Then he again led squads straight across rebel boats and enveloped them along both banks.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove squadrons straight through the enemy line and enveloped them from both shores.

sentences.zh: 出襄河口，斷鐵鎖浮橋，毀北岸火藥庫，仍入襄河。

translations.literal: Emerging at Xianghekou, they severed the iron chains and floating bridge, destroyed the north-bank powder magazine, and re-entered the Xiang River.
translations.idiomatic: Breaking out at Xianghekou, they cut the chained pontoon bridge, blew up the north-bank powder magazine, and fought back into the Xiang River.

sentences.zh: 乘夜撲漢陽，擒賊酋蕭朝富、吳會元。

translations.literal: By night they stormed Hanyang and captured the rebel chiefs Xiao Chaofu and Wu Huiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In a night assault on Hanyang they captured rebel leaders Xiao Chaofu and Wu Huiyuan.

sentences.zh: 麾軍攻拔五顯廟，毀晴川閣木城，又破之葉家洲，燒賊船二百餘。

translations.literal: He commanded the army to storm and take Wuxianmiao, destroyed the wooden fort at Qingchuan Pavilion, broke them again at Yejiachou, and burned more than two hundred rebel boats.
translations.idiomatic: His troops stormed Wuxianmiao, demolished the wooden fort at Qingchuan Pavilion, routed the rebels again at Yejiachou, and burned more than two hundred boats.

sentences.zh: 初由沙口移軍沌口，過經賊壘，砲如雨下，所乘船桅折覆水。

translations.literal: When he first moved his army from Shakou to Dunkou, passing rebel fortifications, cannon fire fell like rain and the boat he rode had its mast broken and capsized in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Moving from Shakou to Dunkou he passed rebel batteries under a rain of shot; his own vessel lost its mast and capsized.

sentences.zh: 玉麟援橫枚漂江中流，楊岳斌舟掠過，掉舢板拯之還。

translations.literal: Yulin clung to a crossbeam and drifted midstream; Yang Yuebin's boat swept past, turned a sampan, and rescued him back.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin grabbed a spar and drifted midstream until Yang Yuebin's boat swept past, sent a sampan, and pulled him out.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼疏陳稱其忠勇冠軍，膽識沈毅，詔以道員記名。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi memorialized, praising his loyalty and courage as foremost in the army and his boldness and steadiness; an edict registered him for appointment as circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi memorialized that Yulin's loyalty and courage topped the army and his judgment under fire was unmatched; the throne registered him for appointment as circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 時曾國籓在江西，水軍頻挫，迭召往助。

translations.literal: At that time Zeng Guofan was in Jiangxi; the navy suffered repeated setbacks and repeatedly summoned Yulin to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan was then in Jiangxi, where the fleet kept taking losses and repeatedly called Yulin to help.

sentences.zh: 玉麟乞假回長沙，急赴之。

translations.literal: Yulin asked leave to return to Changsha and hurried to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin secured leave to return to Changsha and raced to join him.

sentences.zh: 袁、瑞兩郡並陷賊，水陸道絕，易衣裝為賈客，徒步數百里達南昌。

translations.literal: Yuan and Rui prefectures had both fallen to rebels; land and water routes were cut off; he changed clothes to dress as a merchant and walked several hundred li to reach Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: With Yuan and Rui prefectures in rebel hands and every route cut, he disguised himself as a merchant and walked hundreds of li to reach Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 重整內湖水師為十營，船六百艘。

translations.literal: He reorganized the inner-lake navy into ten battalions with six hundred boats.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the inner-lake fleet as ten battalions with six hundred boats.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢廣東惠潮嘉道。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to circuit intendant of Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jiaying in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he was promoted to intendant of the Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jiaying circuit in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 敗賊樟樹鎮，又連破之於臨江吳城、塗家埠，克南康。

translations.literal: He defeated the rebels at Zhangshu Town and again repeatedly broke them at Wucheng and Tujiabu in Linjiang, and took Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the rebels at Zhangshu Town, won again at Wucheng and Tujiabu near Linjiang, and captured Nankang.

sentences.zh: 七年，國籓還籍治父喪，玉麟與楊岳斌同領其軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Guofan returned home to observe mourning for his father; Yulin and Yang Yuebin jointly commanded his army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 Zeng Guofan went home for his father's mourning, leaving Yulin and Yang Yuebin in joint command.

sentences.zh: 其秋，武、漢再克，水陸並下，圍九江。

translations.literal: That autumn Wuchang and Hankou were recovered again; land and water forces advanced together and besieged Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Wuchang and Hankou were retaken again; land and river forces drove down together and besieged Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 玉麟約岳斌夾攻湖口，賊扼石鐘山、梅家洲，力遏內湖軍不得出。

translations.literal: Yulin arranged with Yuebin for a pincer attack on Hukou; the rebels held Shizhongshan and Meijiazhou and forcefully blocked the inner-lake fleet from getting out.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin and Yuebin planned a pincer on Hukou, but rebels holding Shizhongshan and Meijiazhou blocked the inner-lake fleet.

sentences.zh: 玉麟分軍為三以進，賊穴山腹置巨砲，直船衝，舢板先出，前鋒中砲，後船繼進，傷十餘艘。

translations.literal: Yulin divided his army into three columns to advance; the rebels tunneled into the mountain belly and placed huge cannon; they charged straight at the boats; sampans went out first; the vanguard was hit by cannon; succeeding boats pressed on and more than ten were damaged.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin split his force into three columns; rebels had burrowed guns into the hillside and blasted the lead sampans, damaging more than ten boats as the rest pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 玉麟憤曰：「此險不破，萬不令將士獨死，亦不使怯者獨生！」

translations.literal: Yulin said angrily: "If this strongpoint is not broken, I will never let officers and men die alone, nor let the timid live alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Yulin cried in anger, "Unless this strongpoint falls, I will not let brave men die alone while cowards live!"

sentences.zh: 鼓棹急赴，賊砲忽裂，船銜尾下，與外江水師合，歡聲雷動。

translations.literal: He beat the oars and rushed forward; a rebel cannon suddenly burst; boats followed one after another downstream and joined the outer-river navy; cheers thundered.
translations.idiomatic: He drove his boat forward; a rebel gun exploded; the squadron surged downstream, joined the outer fleet, and cheers shook the river.

sentences.zh: 陸軍由城背山下應之，賊大奔，乘勝奪小孤山，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: The land army responded from below the city on the mountain rear; the rebels fled in great disorder; they seized the victory and took Xiaogushan; he was given the rank of surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Infantry answered from the slopes behind the city; the rebels broke and fled; the allies took Xiaogushan, and Yulin received the rank of surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年，連破樅陽、大通、銅陵、峽口賊屯，合圍九江，克之，晉布政使銜。

translations.literal: In the eighth year they repeatedly broke rebel encampments at Zongyang, Datong, Tongling, and Xiakou, combined siege on Jiujiang, and took it; he was advanced to vice governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 the fleet smashed rebel camps at Zongyang, Datong, Tongling, and Xiakou, joined the siege of Jiujiang, and took the city; Yulin was promoted to vice governor.

sentences.zh: 楊岳斌進軍黃石磯，自九江至武昌，置十二屯。

translations.literal: Yang Yuebin advanced to Huangshiji; from Jiujiang to Wuchang he established twelve encampments.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuebin pushed to Huangshiji and planted twelve camps from Jiujiang to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 十年，玉麟移營與合屯。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Yulin moved his camp to join the combined encampment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 Yulin shifted camp to join the combined anchorage.

sentences.zh: 賊复上犯彭澤、湖口，分兵赴援，克都昌。

translations.literal: Rebels again advanced upstream against Pengze and Hukou; he divided forces to reinforce and took Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels again drove upstream toward Pengze and Hukou; he sent detachments, relieved the pressure, and captured Duchang.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授廣東按察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed surveillance commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he was appointed surveillance commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 賊犯蘄、黃、德安，玉麟會陸軍克孝感、天門、應城、黃州、德安，擢安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: Rebels invaded Qizhou, Huangzhou, and De'an; Yulin joined the land army in taking Xiaogan, Tianmen, Yingcheng, Huangzhou, and De'an, and was promoted to governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels struck Qizhou, Huangzhou, and De'an, Yulin coordinated with land forces to recover Xiaogan, Tianmen, Yingcheng, Huangzhou, and De'an, and was promoted governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 命幫辦袁甲三軍務，潁、壽各軍悉歸調遣，累疏固辭，謂：「久居戰艦，草衣短笠，日與水勇、舵工馳逐於巨風惡浪之中。

translations.literal: He was ordered to assist in Yuan Jiasan's military affairs; all armies in Ying and Shou were placed under his command; he repeatedly memorialized firmly declining, saying: "For long I have lived on warships, in straw cloak and bamboo hat, daily racing with sailors and helmsmen through great winds and wicked waves.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to assist Yuan Jiasan's campaigns with every army in Yingzhou and Shouzhou under his command, he repeatedly refused, writing, "For years I have lived aboard warships in straw cloak and bamboo hat, racing with sailors and helmsmen through storms.

sentences.zh: 一旦身膺疆寄，進退百僚，問錢穀不知，問刑名不知，勉強負荷，貽誤國家。」

translations.literal: Once I bear frontier responsibility, advancing and retreating among a hundred officials, asked about revenue and grain I do not know, asked about penal matters I do not know; if I force myself to bear the burden, I will bring harm to the state."
translations.idiomatic: If I suddenly become a frontier governor, directing a hundred officials yet knowing nothing of revenue or criminal law, I would only harm the state by accepting."

sentences.zh: 又謂：「從軍八年，專帶水師，棄舟而陸，無一旅一將供其指揮，倉猝召募，必致僨事。」

translations.literal: He also said: "In eight years with the army I have commanded only the navy; abandoning boats for land I have not one brigade or one general under my command; if hurriedly recruited, disaster is sure to follow."
translations.idiomatic: After eight years commanding only river forces, I have no infantry brigade or general to command on land; hurried recruitment would invite disaster."

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其不欺，以李續宜代之，改職水師提督​​。

translations.literal: An edict praised his honesty; Li Xuyi replaced him; his post was changed to commander of the navy.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised his honesty, replaced him with Li Xuyi, and made him commander of the navy.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，授兵部右侍郎，節制鎮將。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was appointed vice minister of the Board of War and given authority over garrison generals.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was appointed vice minister of war with authority over garrison generals.

sentences.zh: 軍中重文輕武，玉麟與楊岳斌威望久埒，一旦名位超越，​​而相處終始無間，論者謂其苦心協和不可及。

translations.literal: In the army civil officials were valued above military ones; Yulin and Yang Yuebin had long enjoyed equal prestige; once rank and title surpassed others, yet in their dealings from beginning to end there was no breach; commentators said their painstaking harmony was beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: The army still favored scholars over soldiers, yet though Yulin now outranked Yang Yuebin, whom he had long matched in prestige, the two never quarreled—a harmony commentators called impossible to imitate.

sentences.zh: 別立太湖水師十營，並歸統轄。

translations.literal: He separately established ten battalions of the Taihu navy, all placed under his overall command.
translations.idiomatic: He also formed ten Taihu Lake battalions placed under his overall command.

sentences.zh: 曾國荃由安慶進規江寧，水師助之。

translations.literal: Zeng Guoquan advanced from Anqing toward Jiangning; the navy assisted.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guoquan advanced from Anqing toward Nanjing with naval support.

sentences.zh: 克銅城閘，复巢縣、含山、和州，襲破雍家鎮、裕溪口，奪東西梁山，進攻採石，又克金柱關。

translations.literal: They took Tongcheng Pass, recovered Chaoxian, Hanshan, and Hezhou, raided and broke Yongjia Town and Yuxikou, seized the eastern and western Liangshan, advanced on Caishi, and again took Jinzhuguan.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet captured Tongcheng Pass, retook Chaoxian, Hanshan, and Hezhou, stormed Yongjia Town and Yuxikou, seized East and West Liangshan, advanced on Caishi, and took Jinzhuguan.

sentences.zh: 諸將衝鋒，玉麟每乘小船督戰，以紅旗為識，或前或後，將士皆惴惴盡力。

translations.literal: When generals charged, Yulin each time rode a small boat to direct battle, using a red flag as his mark; sometimes ahead, sometimes behind; officers and men all trembled and exerted themselves to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: While other generals led charges, Yulin directed battle from a small boat marked by a red flag, appearing now ahead and now astern until every sailor fought with desperate energy.

sentences.zh: 間入陸軍察戰狀，往來飄忽無定踪，所經行軍民莫敢為奸宄。

translations.literal: At times he entered the land army to observe the battle situation, coming and going elusive without fixed trace; wherever he passed, soldiers and civilians dared not commit wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: He sometimes slipped ashore to inspect the land battle, appearing and vanishing unpredictably; wherever he passed, soldiers and civilians dared not misconduct themselves.

sentences.zh: 二年，與楊岳斌合兵攻九洑洲。

translations.literal: In the second year he joined Yang Yuebin in combined attack on Jiufuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he and Yang Yuebin jointly assaulted Jiufuzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊於洲築壘數十，外作大城，眾舟環之，與江寧相犄角；

translations.literal: The rebels built dozens of fortifications on the islet, with a great outer wall; many boats ringed it, forming horns with Jiangning;
translations.idiomatic: Rebels fortified the islet with dozens of camps inside a great outer wall, ringed by boats that linked defenses with Nanjing;

sentences.zh: 而攔江磯、草鞋峽、七里洲、燕子磯、中關、下關皆賊屯。

translations.literal: while Lanjiangji, Caoxiexia, Qilizhou, Yanziji, Zhongguan, and Xiaguan were all rebel encampments.
translations.idiomatic: Lanjiangji, Caoxiexia, Qilizhou, Yanziji, Zhongguan, and Xiaguan were all held by rebel camps.

sentences.zh: 玉麟列舟上流，南隊向下關，北隊向草鞋峽，岳斌攻燕子磯，破之。

translations.literal: Yulin arrayed boats upstream; the southern squadron moved on Xiaguan and the northern on Caoxiexia; Yuebin attacked Yanziji and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin lined boats upstream: the southern squadron struck Xiaguan, the northern Caoxiexia, while Yuebin stormed Yanziji and broke through.

sentences.zh: 陸軍亦分三隊，掘洲埂攻中關，舢板環洲而陣。

translations.literal: The land army also divided into three squads, digging through the islet embankment to attack Zhongguan; sampans ringed the islet in formation.
translations.idiomatic: Land forces split three ways, digging through the islet dike toward Zhongguan while sampans ringed the shore in battle line.

sentences.zh: 賊以槍砲相持，不能進。

translations.literal: Rebels matched them with muskets and cannon and could not be advanced upon.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel musketry and cannon held the allies at bay.

sentences.zh: 玉麟督諸軍更番夜攻，下令曰：「洲不破，不收隊。」

translations.literal: Yulin directed the armies in rotating night attacks and ordered: "Until the islet is broken, do not withdraw the squadrons."
translations.idiomatic: Yulin ordered rotating night assaults with the command, "Do not recall the squadrons until the islet falls."

sentences.zh: 選死士從火叢登岸，噪曰：「洲破矣！」

translations.literal: He selected death-defying men to climb ashore through the flames and clamored: "The islet is broken!"
translations.idiomatic: He sent volunteers through the fire to the shore, shouting, "The islet is taken!"

sentences.zh: 諸軍歡呼，騰踔而上，立破洲邊屯舟，賊爭潰走。

translations.literal: The armies cheered, leaped and scrambled upward, immediately broke the encampments and boats on the islet edge, and the rebels all fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Cheers erupted; men leaped ashore, smashed the riverside camps and boats, and the rebels broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 自田家鎮以來，是戰為最烈。

translations.literal: Since Tianjiazhen this battle had been the fiercest.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tianjiazhen, no battle had been fiercer.

sentences.zh: 於是賊黨由江西犯池州，謀撓官軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon rebel bands from Jiangxi invaded Chizhou, plotting to harass the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel bands from Jiangxi then struck Chizhou, hoping to disrupt the government offensive.

sentences.zh: 玉麟還救青陽，解其圍，復高淳，克東壩，並論九洑洲功，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Yulin returned to relieve Qingyang, lifted the siege, recovered Gaochun, took Dongba, and for merit at Jiufuzhou was granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin raced back to relieve Qingyang, lifted the siege, retook Gaochun and captured Dongba; for Jiufuzhou he received the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 會楊岳斌赴江西督師，自是玉麟專統水師。

translations.literal: When Yang Yuebin went to Jiangxi to command armies, from then on Yulin alone commanded the navy.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yuebin left to command in Jiangxi, Yulin alone commanded the river fleet.

sentences.zh: 三年，江寧复，論功，以創立水師為首，加太子少保，予一等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: In the third year Jiangning was recovered; for merit, founding the navy was ranked first; he was given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the hereditary rank of First Class Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell in 1864, founding the navy was ranked his foremost merit; he became Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the hereditary rank of First Class Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 四年，命署漕運總督，再疏辭，允之，命籌商水師善後事宜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was ordered to act as Director-General of Grain Transport; he memorialized again to decline; this was granted; he was ordered to plan postwar arrangements for the navy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he was ordered to serve as acting grain-transport director, declined again, was excused, and was told to plan the navy's postwar settlement.

sentences.zh: 七年，會同曾國籓奏定長江水師營製，自荊州至崇明五千餘裡，設提督一員、總兵五員，以六標分汛；

translations.literal: In the seventh year, together with Zeng Guofan he memorialized to fix the organization of the Yangtze navy, from Jingzhou to Chongming over five thousand li, establishing one commander, five major generals, and six flotillas for patrol;
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he and Zeng Guofan fixed the Yangtze navy's organization from Jingzhou to Chongming—more than five thousand li—with one commander, five major generals, and six patrol flotillas;

sentences.zh: 營、哨官七百九十八員，兵丁一萬二千人，歲餉六十餘萬兩，以長江釐稅供支，不煩戶部。

translations.literal: seven hundred ninety-eight battalion and outpost officers, twelve thousand soldiers, annual pay of more than six hundred thousand taels, supplied from Yangtze transit duties without troubling the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: 798 battalion and outpost officers, twelve thousand men, and annual pay above six hundred thousand taels, all funded from Yangtze transit levies without calling on the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 初，軍事未定，軍餉奇絀，而淮鹽積滯。

translations.literal: At first, while military affairs were unsettled, army pay was desperately short and Huai salt piled up unsold.
translations.idiomatic: While the war still raged, army pay ran desperately short and Huai salt piled up unsold.

sentences.zh: 玉麟議定捆鹽自賣，供水師月餉。

translations.literal: Yulin proposed fixing bundled salt for self-sale to supply the navy's monthly pay.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin proposed selling bundled salt on the fleet's own account to meet monthly navy pay.

sentences.zh: 及江路大通，曾國籓設三省督銷局，招商領票，水師鹽票大小數百，至是軍餉有額支的款。

translations.literal: When the river route was fully open, Zeng Guofan established a three-province supervisory sales bureau, inviting merchants to take tickets; the navy's salt tickets numbered in the hundreds large and small; then army pay had fixed disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: Once the river reopened, Zeng Guofan opened a three-province salt bureau where merchants bought tickets; the navy held hundreds of salt tickets, and pay finally had a fixed source.

sentences.zh: 餘銀及票本巨萬，玉麟一不私取，以五之一取息，助水師公費，且備外患倉猝之需。

translations.literal: Surplus silver and ticket capital amounted to tens of thousands; Yulin took not one tael for himself; with one-fifth taken as interest he assisted navy public expenses and also prepared for sudden external emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus silver and ticket capital ran to tens of thousands of taels; Yulin kept none for himself, using one-fifth of the interest for fleet expenses and a reserve against sudden emergencies.

sentences.zh: 餘分解雲、貴助餉二十萬，甘肅助餉二十萬，以十萬廣本縣學額，而以鹽票犒諸將有大功者。

translations.literal: The remainder he divided: two hundred thousand to assist pay in Yunnan and Guizhou, two hundred thousand to assist pay in Gansu, one hundred thousand to expand quotas at his home county school, and with salt tickets rewarded generals of great merit.
translations.idiomatic: He sent two hundred thousand taels each to Yunnan-Guizhou and Gansu pay chests, ten thousand to expand his home county's school quota, and rewarded distinguished generals with salt tickets.

sentences.zh: 事既竣，疏請回籍補行終制，略曰：「臣墨絰從戎，創立水師，治軍十餘年，未嘗營一瓦之覆，一畝之殖；

translations.literal: When matters were concluded he memorialized asking to return home to complete the mourning period, stating in summary: "Your servant, in hemp mourning, followed the army, founded the navy, and governed troops for more than ten years without ever building one tile of shelter or cultivating one mu of land;
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done he asked to go home and complete mourning, writing in part, "I joined the army still in mourning dress, founded the navy, and commanded troops for more than ten years without building a roof or planting a field;

sentences.zh: 受傷積勞，未嘗請一日之假；

translations.literal: injured and worn by accumulated labor, he never asked one day's leave;
translations.idiomatic: wounded and worn by years of labor, I never asked a single day's leave;

sentences.zh: 終年風濤矢石之中，未嘗移居岸上求一日之安。

translations.literal: throughout the year amid wind, waves, and arrows and stones, he never moved ashore to seek one day's peace.
translations.idiomatic: year-round I lived among wind, waves, arrows, and shot without moving ashore for a day's peace.

sentences.zh: 誠以親服未終，而出從戎旅，既難免不孝之罪，豈敢復為身家之圖乎？

translations.literal: Truly because mourning for his parent was not yet complete yet he went out to follow the army, he could hardly escape the crime of unfiliality—how could he dare again to scheme for his own household?
translations.idiomatic: Having left home before mourning ended, I can hardly escape the charge of unfiliality—how then could I scheme for my own household?

sentences.zh: 臣嘗聞士大夫出處進退，關係風俗之盛衰。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that whether scholar-officials advance or withdraw concerns the rise and fall of custom.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when scholar-officials advance or withdraw without propriety, custom itself declines.

sentences.zh: 臣之從戎，志在滅賊，賊己滅而不歸，近於貪位；

translations.literal: Your servant's joining the army aimed at destroying rebels; once rebels were destroyed yet he did not return, this approaches greed for office;
translations.idiomatic: I joined the army to destroy the rebels; with the rebels gone yet I stay on, I seem greedy for office;

sentences.zh: 長江既設提鎮，臣猶在軍，近於戀權；

translations.literal: the Yangtze already had commanders and major generals yet your servant still remained with the army, this approaches clinging to power;
translations.idiomatic: with Yangtze commanders already appointed yet I remain with the fleet, I seem to cling to power;

sentences.zh: 改易初心，貪戀權位，則前此辭官，疑是作偽；

translations.literal: if he changed his original intent and greedily clung to rank and power, then his earlier resignations would be suspected as pretense;
translations.idiomatic: if I now change my mind and cling to rank, my earlier resignations will look like pretense;

sentences.zh: 三年之制，賢愚所同，軍事已終，仍不補行終制，久留於外，涉於忘親。

translations.literal: the three-year mourning rule is the same for wise and foolish alike; military affairs were already ended yet he still did not complete mourning at home, long remaining abroad, which touches on forgetting parents.
translations.idiomatic: the three-year mourning rule binds wise and foolish alike; with the war ended yet I still refuse to mourn at home, I neglect my parents.

sentences.zh: 四者有一，皆足以傷風敗俗。

translations.literal: If any one of the four were present, each would suffice to harm custom and ruin morals.
translations.idiomatic: Any one of these four faults would harm public morals.

sentences.zh: 夫天下之亂，不徒在盜賊之未平，而在士大夫之進無禮，退無義。

translations.literal: The disorder of the realm lies not only in rebels not yet pacified, but in scholar-officials advancing without ritual and withdrawing without righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The empire's disorder lies not only in unpacified rebels but in officials who advance without ritual and withdraw without righteousness.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇上中興大業，正宜扶樹名教，整肅紀綱，以振起人心。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully considers that in the Emperor's great work of restoration, it is precisely fitting to uphold the teaching of names, rectify discipline, and revive the hearts of men.
translations.idiomatic: In Your Majesty's restoration, this is the moment to uphold moral teaching, tighten discipline, and revive men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 況人之才力聰明，用久則竭，若不善藏其短，必致轉失所長。

translations.literal: Moreover human talent, strength, and intelligence, used long, are exhausted; if one does not know well how to hide one's shortcomings, one will surely turn and lose what one excels at.
translations.idiomatic: Talent and vigor exhaust themselves with long use; those who cannot hide their weaknesses eventually lose their strengths.

sentences.zh: 古來臣子，往往初年頗有建樹，而晚節末路隕越錯謬，固由才庸，亦其精氣竭也。

translations.literal: Ministers and subjects of old often in early years achieved much, yet in late years and at life's end stumbled into error and mistake; though partly from mediocre talent, their vital spirit was also exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: History shows many men who achieved much in youth yet stumbled in old age—not only from mediocrity but from spent vigor.

sentences.zh: 臣每讀史至此，竊歎其人不能善藏其短，又惜當日朝廷不知善全其長。

translations.literal: Your servant, reading history to this point, privately sighs that such men could not well hide their shortcomings, and also regrets that the court of that day did not know how well to preserve their strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Reading such histories I sigh that they could not hide their flaws, and regret that their courts failed to preserve their gifts.

sentences.zh: 知進而不知退，聖人於易深戒之，固有由矣。

translations.literal: Knowing advance yet not knowing withdrawal—the sage in the Changes deeply warns of this; there is indeed reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes warn that knowing when to advance yet not when to withdraw brings ruin—and with good reason.

sentences.zh: 臣本無經濟之學，而性情褊躁，思慮憂傷。

translations.literal: Your servant originally had no learning in statecraft, and by nature is narrow and impatient; in thought he is anxious and sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: I have no gift for statecraft, my temper is narrow and impatient, and worry weighs on me.

sentences.zh: 月積年累，怔忡眴暈，精力日衰，心氣日耗。

translations.literal: Month piled on month and year on year, palpitations and dizziness accumulate; vital energy daily declines and heart-spirit daily wastes.
translations.idiomatic: Month after month palpitations and dizziness accumulate; my strength and spirit waste away.

sentences.zh: 若再不調理，必致貽誤國事。

translations.literal: If he is not again regulated and cared for, he will surely bring harm to state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Without rest I will surely harm state affairs.

sentences.zh: 懇請天恩開臣兵部侍郎本缺，回籍補行終制。

translations.literal: He earnestly requests Heaven's grace to open your servant's substantive post as vice minister of the Board of War and allow return home to complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to release me from the substantive post of vice minister of war and allow me to return home and complete mourning.

sentences.zh: 報國之日正長，斷不敢永圖安逸也。」

translations.literal: The day of serving the state is still long; he absolutely dares not forever seek ease and comfort."
translations.idiomatic: My days of service are still long; I do not seek permanent ease."

sentences.zh: 優詔從之。

translations.literal: A gracious edict granted this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of grace granted his request.

sentences.zh: 八年春，還衡陽，作草樓三重，布衣青鞋，時往母墓，廬居三年不出。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year he returned to Hengyang, built a three-story thatched pavilion, wore plain cloth and blue shoes, and from time to time went to his mother's tomb; he lived in a hut for three years without going out.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1869 he returned to Hengyang, built a three-story thatched retreat, dressed in plain cloth and blue shoes, visited his mother's tomb, and lived in mourning seclusion for three years.

sentences.zh: 自設長江水師，東南無事，將士漸耽安逸，事多廢弛。

translations.literal: Since the Yangtze navy was established, the southeast was at peace; officers and men gradually indulged in ease; many affairs fell into neglect.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yangtze navy was established the southeast knew peace, and officers and men slowly grew lax as discipline slackened.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔起玉麟簡閱，疏陳整頓事宜，諷提督黃翼升自退，薦李成謀、彭楚漢二人，即以成謀代之，劾罷營哨官百數十人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an edict recalled Yulin for inspection; he memorialized on measures for rectification, indirectly urging Commander Huang Yisheng to retire, recommended Li Chengmo and Peng Chuhan, and had Chengmo replace him; he impeached and dismissed more than a hundred battalion and outpost officers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1872 an edict recalled Yulin to inspect the fleet; he memorialized on reform, nudging Commander Huang Yisheng to retire, recommending Li Chengmo and Peng Chuhan to replace him, and cashiered more than a hundred battalion and outpost officers.

sentences.zh: 入覲，命署兵部侍郎，复陳請開缺，仍命巡閱長江，專摺奏事。

translations.literal: On entering audience he was ordered to act as vice minister of the Board of War; he again memorialized asking to vacate the post; he was still ordered to inspect the Yangtze and report by memorial alone.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he was again ordered to act as vice minister of war, declined once more, and was told to keep inspecting the Yangtze and reporting by memorial.

sentences.zh: 別飭兩江、湖廣為籌經費，玉效力辭不受。

translations.literal: Separately the Two Jiangs and Huguang were ordered to raise funds; Yulin vigorously declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Two Jiangs and Huguang were ordered to raise funds for him, but he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 自築別業於杭州西湖，曰退省庵。

translations.literal: He built a separate estate on West Lake at Hangzhou called the Retreat-for-Reflection Hermitage.
translations.idiomatic: He built a retreat on Hangzhou's West Lake called the Hermitage of Retreat and Reflection.

sentences.zh: 每巡閱下游，事畢，居之。

translations.literal: Each time he inspected downstream and when affairs were finished, he lived there.
translations.idiomatic: After each downstream inspection he returned to live there.

sentences.zh: 自是水師皆整肅，沿江盜踪斂戢，安堵者數十年。

translations.literal: From then on the navy was all disciplined; river pirates along the banks were subdued; peace lasted for several decades.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the fleet remained disciplined, river piracy subsided, and decades passed in peace.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有大政，及疆吏重案，輒諮詢，命按治。

translations.literal: When the court had great policies, or frontier officials had weighty cases, it repeatedly consulted him and ordered him to investigate and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: On major court policies and weighty frontier cases the throne repeatedly sought his judgment and sent him to investigate.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，命署兩江總督，再疏力辭，乃以左宗棠代之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu he was ordered to act as Governor-General of the Two Jiangs; he memorialized again with all his strength to decline; then Zuo Zongtang replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 he was ordered to act as governor-general of the Two Jiangs, declined with all his force, and Zuo Zongtang was appointed instead.

sentences.zh: 留督江、海防如故。

translations.literal: He remained in charge of river and coastal defense as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was kept on to oversee river and coastal defenses, just as before.

sentences.zh: 言者議長江提督宜駐吳淞口外，玉麟疏言：「江南提督責在海防，請多畀兵輪，使立一軍於海上。

translations.literal: Critics debated that the Yangtze commander should be stationed outside Wusongkou; Yulin memorialized, saying: "The Jiangnan commander is responsible for coastal defense; please assign more gunboats and establish one army on the sea.
translations.idiomatic: When critics argued the Yangtze commander should move outside Wusong, Yulin wrote, "The Jiangnan commander answers for coastal defense—give him gunboats and establish a sea force.

sentences.zh: 長江提督責在江防，請仍由臣督同巡閱，改駐吳淞，會操兵輪，以通江、海。」

translations.literal: The Yangtze commander is responsible for river defense; please still have your servant supervise joint inspection, change station to Wusong, and drill gunboats together to connect river and sea."
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze commander answers for river defense—let me continue joint inspection from Wusong, drilling gunboats to link river and sea."

sentences.zh: 九年，擢兵部尚書，以衰病辭。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to minister of the Board of War and declined on account of age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1883 he was promoted to minister of war but declined on grounds of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 會法、越構兵，命赴廣東會籌防務。

translations.literal: When France and Vietnam went to war, he was ordered to go to Guangdong to join in planning defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Franco-Vietnamese war broke out, he was ordered to Guangdong to help plan coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 玉麟募四千人從行，駐大黃。

translations.literal: Yulin recruited four thousand men to accompany him and encamped at Dahuang.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin raised four thousand men, marched with them, and encamped at Dahuang.

sentences.zh: 遣部將王之春、黃得勝等防瓊州、欽州、靈山，婁雲慶、王永章等駐沙角、大角，與粵軍聯合。

translations.literal: He sent subordinates Wang Zhichun and Huang Desheng to defend Qiongzhou, Qinzhou, and Lingshan; Lou Yunqing and Wang Yongzhang encamped at Shajiao and Dajiao, coordinating with Guangdong forces.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates Wang Zhichun and Huang Desheng guarded Qiongzhou, Qinzhou, and Lingshan; Lou Yunqing and Wang Yongzhang held Shajiao and Dajiao alongside Guangdong troops.

sentences.zh: 增兵設壘，編沙戶漁舟，分守內沙港汊。

translations.literal: He increased troops and built fortifications, registered sand households and fishing boats, and divided defense of inner sand harbors and channels.
translations.idiomatic: He added troops and forts, registered sand-dwellers and fishing boats, and divided patrol of inner sand channels.

sentences.zh: 法兵竟不至。

translations.literal: French troops in the end did not come.
translations.idiomatic: French troops never came.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，粵軍大捷於鎮南關，進攻諒山。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year the Guangdong army won a great victory at Zhennanguan and advanced to attack Langshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1885 the Guangdong army won a great victory at Zhennanguan and advanced on Langshan.

sentences.zh: 和議旋成，停戰撤兵。

translations.literal: Peace talks were soon concluded; fighting stopped and troops were withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Peace was quickly negotiated, fighting stopped, and troops withdrew.

sentences.zh: 玉麟疏請嚴備戰守，以毖後患，陳海防善後六事。

translations.literal: Yulin memorialized asking for strict preparation of war and defense to guard against later trouble, setting forth six matters for postwar coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin memorialized for strict readiness against future trouble and laid out six points on postwar coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 是秋，以病乞休，溫詔慰留。

translations.literal: That autumn he asked leave on account of illness; a warm edict comforted him and kept him in post.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he asked to retire for illness; a warm edict comforted him and kept him in service.

sentences.zh: 十四年，扶病巡閱。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he inspected while leaning on illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1888 he conducted an inspection despite illness.

sentences.zh: 至安慶，巡撫陳彝見其病篤，以聞，詔允開缺回籍，仍留巡閱差使。

translations.literal: Reaching Anqing, Governor Chen Yi, seeing his illness grave, reported this; an edict granted vacating his substantive post and returning home, yet still retaining the inspection assignment.
translations.idiomatic: At Anqing, Governor Chen Yi, seeing him gravely ill, reported it; the throne released him from substantive office but kept him on inspection duty.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒，年七十五，贈太子太保，依尚書例賜卹，建專祠立功地，諡剛直。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died, aged seventy-five; he was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, condolence payments according to the precedent for a minister, a special shrine at the place of his merit, and the posthumous name Gangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1890 he died at seventy-five; the court posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted ministerial mourning payments, built a shrine where he had served, and gave the posthumous name Gangzhi, "Unyielding and Upright."

sentences.zh: 玉麟剛介絕俗，素厭文法，治事輒得法外意。

translations.literal: Yulin was rigid and aloof from common ways, always disliking legal formalities; in handling affairs he often grasped the intent beyond the letter of law.
translations.idiomatic: Rigid and indifferent to convention, Yulin disliked legal formalism yet usually grasped the spirit of the law in judgment.

sentences.zh: 不通權貴，而坦易直亮，無傾軋倨傲之心。

translations.literal: He did not cultivate the powerful, yet was open, easy, straight, and bright, without a heart of undermining or arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: He shunned the powerful yet was frank, approachable, and upright, without jealousy or arrogance.

sentences.zh: 歷奉命按重臣疆吏被劾者，於左宗棠、劉坤一、塗宗瀛、張樹聲等，皆主持公道，務存大體，亦不為谿刻。

translations.literal: Repeatedly ordered to investigate great ministers and frontier officials who had been impeached—among Zuo Zongtang, Liu Kunyi, Tu Zongying, and Zhang Shusheng—he always upheld justice, sought to preserve the larger pattern, and was not petty.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating impeached great ministers such as Zuo Zongtang, Liu Kunyi, Tu Zongying, and Zhang Shusheng, he upheld justice, preserved the larger interest, and avoided pettiness.

sentences.zh: 每出巡，偵官吏不法輒劾懲，甚者以軍法斬之然後聞，故所至官吏皆危栗。

translations.literal: Each time he went on inspection, if he detected unlawful officials he impeached and punished them; in severe cases he executed by military law and then reported; therefore wherever he arrived officials all trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: On inspection he impeached corrupt officials and, in grave cases, executed them by military law before reporting—so officials trembled wherever he appeared.

sentences.zh: 民有枉，往往盼彭公來。

translations.literal: When the people suffered injustice, they often hoped Peng Gong would come.
translations.idiomatic: When common people suffered injustice they often prayed for Lord Peng to come.

sentences.zh: 朝廷傾心聽之，不居位而京察屢加褒獎，倚畀蓋過於疆吏。

translations.literal: The court listened to him with full trust; though he did not hold office, in repeated capital evaluations he was repeatedly praised and rewarded; reliance on him exceeded that on frontier governors.
translations.idiomatic: The court trusted him completely; though out of office, repeated capital evaluations praised him, and the throne relied on him more than on sitting governors.

sentences.zh: 生平奏牘皆手裁，每出，為世傳誦。

translations.literal: Throughout his life his memorials were all written by his own hand; each time one appeared it was transmitted and recited by the world.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted every memorial himself, and each one circulated widely once issued.

sentences.zh: 好畫梅，詩書皆超俗，文采風流亦不沫雲。

translations.literal: He loved painting plum blossoms; his poetry and calligraphy all surpassed the common; literary grace and spirit likewise did not fall short of the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: He loved painting plum blossoms; his poetry and calligraphy were exceptional, and his literary grace was no less admired.

sentences.zh: =楊岳斌=楊岳斌，原名載福，字厚庵，湖南善化人，原籍乾州。

translations.literal: Biography of Yang Yuebin. Yang Yuebin, original name Zaifu, styled Hou'an, was a native of Shanhua in Hunan, with ancestral home in Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Yang Yuebin. Yang Yuebin, originally named Zaifu and styled Hou'an, came from Shanhua in Hunan; his ancestral home was Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖勝德，乾隆末，從剿苗，戰歿永綏。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shengde, in the late Qianlong reign, followed campaigns against the Miao and died in battle at Yongshui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shengde campaigned against the Miao in the late Qianlong reign and was killed at Yongshui.

sentences.zh: 父秀貴，以廕官至直隸獨石口副將。

translations.literal: His father Xiugui rose by yin privilege to vice commander at Dushikou in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiugui rose by inherited privilege to vice commander at Dushikou in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 岳斌幼嫺騎射，補湘陰外委，從剿新寧匪。

translations.literal: Yuebin in youth was skilled in horsemanship and archery; he was appointed outside officer in Xiangyin and joined suppression of rebels in Xinning.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yuebin excelled at riding and archery; appointed an outside officer in Xiangyin, he joined the suppression of rebels in Xinning.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，守湘陰有功，擢宜章營千總。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he defended Xiangyin with merit and was promoted to company commander of the Yizhang battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he defended Xiangyin with distinction and was promoted company commander of the Yizhang battalion.

sentences.zh: 三年，曾國籓創立水師，拔為營官。

translations.literal: In the third year Zeng Guofan founded the navy and selected him as battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 Zeng Guofan founded the river fleet and made him a battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 戰岳州，水陸皆潰，獨岳斌一營力拒不敗。

translations.literal: At the battle of Yuezhou, land and water forces all collapsed; only Yuebin's one battalion held firm and was not defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuezhou the land and river forces collapsed; only Yuebin's battalion held and was not broken.

sentences.zh: 四年，戰湘潭，焚賊舟數百，復其城，擢守備，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, at the battle of Xiangtan, they burned hundreds of rebel boats, recovered the city, and he was promoted to battalion commander and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 at Xiangtan he burned hundreds of rebel boats, retook the city, was promoted battalion commander, and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 國籓重整水師，進規岳州。

translations.literal: Guofan reorganized the navy and advanced on Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan reorganized the fleet and advanced on Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 岳斌與彭玉麟為前鋒，伏船雷公湖，誘賊舟至，夾擊，連戰皆捷；

translations.literal: Yuebin and Peng Yulin served as vanguard; they concealed boats at Leigong Lake, lured rebel boats to come, attacked from both sides, and won repeated battles;
translations.idiomatic: Yuebin and Peng Yulin led the vanguard, hid boats at Leigong Lake, lured the rebel fleet out, and won repeated victories in pincer attacks;

sentences.zh: 賊再至，沿東岸斜擊之，手挺矛刺殺賊酋在汪得勝，奪其舟，賊無還者：擢都司，賜號彪勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: when rebels came again, they struck obliquely along the east bank; he personally wielded a spear and killed the rebel chief Zai Wang Desheng, seized his boat, and no rebel returned: he was promoted to battalion commander of the third rank and granted the title Biaoyong Batu.
translations.idiomatic: when rebels returned he struck along the east bank, personally speared the rebel chief Zai Wang Desheng, seized his boat, and cut off every retreat; he was promoted and granted the title Biaoyong Batu.

sentences.zh: 進戰擂鼓台，乘舢板衝賊屯縱火，賊陣亂，大破之，克岳州，擢游擊。

translations.literal: Advancing to battle at Leigutai, he boarded a sampan, charged a rebel encampment and set fire; the rebel formation broke in disorder and was routed; Yuezhou was taken; he was promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: At Leigutai he took a sampan into a rebel camp, set it afire, broke their line, and helped take Yuezhou; he was promoted colonel.

sentences.zh: 總兵陳輝龍率後隊至，狃前勝，欲乘風攻城陵磯。

translations.literal: Major General Chen Huilong led the rear column to arrive; trusting in the earlier victory, he wished to take advantage of the wind to attack Chenglingji.
translations.idiomatic: When Major General Chen Huilong arrived with the rear column, emboldened by earlier victories he wanted to strike Chenglingji with the wind at his back.

sentences.zh: 岳斌曰：「順風難收隊，不可行也。」

translations.literal: Yuebin said: "With a favorable wind it is hard to recall the squadrons; it must not be done."
translations.idiomatic: Yuebin warned, "With this wind you cannot recall the squadrons—it must not be done."

sentences.zh: 不從，遇賊伏，竟敗。

translations.literal: They did not listen; they met a rebel ambush and were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was ignored; they walked into an ambush and were routed.

sentences.zh: 輝龍及知府褚汝航、同知夏鑾、游擊沙鎮邦皆戰死，岳斌軍獨完。

translations.literal: Huilong and Prefect Chu Ruhang, Subprefect Xia Luan, and Colonel Sha Zhenbang all died in battle; Yuebin's army alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong, Prefect Chu Ruhang, Subprefect Xia Luan, and Colonel Sha Zhenbang were killed; only Yuebin's command escaped intact.

sentences.zh: 既而賊為陸師所敗，將遁，要擊之，平兩岸砲台，搜螺山、倒口賊舟。

translations.literal: Soon afterward rebels were defeated by the land army and were about to flee; he intercepted them, leveled batteries on both banks, and searched out rebel boats at Luoshan and Daokou.
translations.idiomatic: When land forces routed fleeing rebels he intercepted them, knocked out shore batteries, and hunted rebel boats at Luoshan and Daokou.

sentences.zh: 尋夜襲嘉魚黃蓋湖，岳斌先入，被火傷，舟覆落水，躍上別船，大呼陷陣，焚賊舟數十。

translations.literal: Soon he raided Huangga Lake at Jiayu by night; Yuebin went in first, was burned by fire, his boat capsized and he fell into the water; he leaped onto another boat, shouted as he plunged into battle, and burned dozens of rebel boats.
translations.idiomatic: In a night raid on Huangga Lake at Jiayu he went in first, was burned, capsized, leaped to another boat, and burned dozens of rebel vessels.

sentences.zh: 遂會湖北軍進屯金口，破漢陽關賊營，攻塘角，至青山，焚其壘，賊遁，焚其輜重。

translations.literal: Then he joined Hubei forces in encamping at Jinkou, broke the rebel camp at Hanyang Pass, attacked Tangjiao, reached Qingshan, burned their fortifications; the rebels fled and he burned their baggage.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Hubei troops at Jinkou, stormed Hanyang Pass, fought through Tangjiao to Qingshan, burned rebel forts, and torched their stores as they fled.

sentences.zh: 武昌、漢陽皆复，擢參將，授湖南常德營副將。

translations.literal: Wuchang and Hanyang were both recovered; he was promoted to brigadier general and appointed vice commander of the Changde battalion in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang and Hanyang were retaken; he became brigadier general and vice commander of the Changde battalion in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 諸軍進規田家鎮，岳斌由中路先發，克黃州及武昌縣，破援賊於蘄州，逼田家鎮，偕彭玉麟分隊毀橫江鐵鎖，焚賊船四千餘皆盡，漂屍數万，遂拔田家鎮，蘄州賊亦遁去。

translations.literal: The armies advanced on Tianjiazhen; Yuebin launched from the center route first, took Huangzhou and Wuchang County, broke relieving rebels at Qizhou, pressed Tianjiazhen, joined Peng Yulin in dividing squads to destroy the iron chains across the river, burned more than four thousand rebel boats completely, corpses numbered in the tens of thousands, then took Tianjiazhen and Qizhou rebels also fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the advance on Tianjiazhen Yuebin led the center, took Huangzhou and Wuchang County, broke Qizhou relief forces, joined Peng Yulin in cutting the river chains, burned more than four thousand boats until corpses numbered in the tens of thousands, and took Tianjiazhen as Qizhou rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 岳斌晝夜進戰，積勞嘔血，詔嘉其勞勚最著，加總兵銜。

translations.literal: Yuebin fought day and night, accumulated exhaustion and vomited blood; an edict praised his labor as most outstanding and added the rank of major general.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting day and night until he vomited blood, he was praised by edict for outstanding service and given major general's rank.

sentences.zh: 五年，水陸會攻九江，岳斌以疾留武穴，尋假歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year land and water forces jointly attacked Jiujiang; Yuebin remained at Wuxue on account of illness and soon asked leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 the combined forces attacked Jiujiang while illness kept Yuebin at Wuxue; he soon went home on leave.

sentences.zh: 水師恃勝銳進，前隊舢板入鄱陽湖，賊樹柵湖口扼之，不得出，而留九江者，亦屢為賊所襲。

translations.literal: The navy, trusting in victory, pressed forward sharply; the vanguard sampans entered Poyang Lake; rebels built palisades at Hukou and blocked them from getting out; those remaining at Jiujiang were also repeatedly raided by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Overconfident after victory, the fleet's lead sampans entered Poyang Lake; rebels walled Hukou and trapped them while Jiujiang detachments were repeatedly raided.

sentences.zh: 岳斌聞敗，馳救不及。

translations.literal: Yuebin heard of the defeat and rushed to rescue but could not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the disaster, Yuebin raced to the rescue but arrived too late.

sentences.zh: 賊复上犯，武、漢再陷。

translations.literal: Rebels again advanced upstream; Wuchang and Hankou fell again.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels drove upstream again and Wuchang and Hankou were lost once more.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓分水師回援，令岳斌回岳州，增募為十營，會屯金口，屢敗賊。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan divided the navy to return in relief and ordered Yuebin back to Yuezhou, increased recruitment to ten battalions, joined encampment at Jinkou, and repeatedly defeated rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan sent part of the fleet back, recalled Yuebin to Yuezhou, rebuilt ten battalions, encamped at Jinkou, and beat the rebels repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 秋，退屯新堤，修船，汰疲卒十之三，簡練以圖大舉。

translations.literal: In autumn he withdrew to Xindi, repaired boats, dismissed one-third of worn-out soldiers, and selected and trained them to plan a major effort.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he withdrew to Xindi, repaired boats, cut a third of the exhausted ranks, and retrained for a major campaign.

sentences.zh: 自武、漢為賊踞，長江商旅皆絕。

translations.literal: Since Wuchang and Hankou were held by rebels, Yangtze merchants and travelers all ceased.
translations.idiomatic: With Wuchang and Hankou in rebel hands, Yangtze commerce stopped entirely.

sentences.zh: 及水師駐新堤，流亡歸之，市廛始興，漸為重鎮。

translations.literal: When the navy encamped at Xindi, exiles returned to it; markets first revived and it gradually became a major town.
translations.idiomatic: When the fleet anchored at Xindi refugees returned, markets revived, and the town gradually became a major base.

sentences.zh: 授鄖陽鎮總兵，兼署湖北提督。

translations.literal: He was appointed major general of Zhenyang garrison and also acted as governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed major general of Zhenyang garrison and acting governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 六年，進屯沙口，距武昌三十里。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he advanced and encamped at Shakou, thirty li from Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he encamped at Shakou, thirty li from Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 岳斌念賊舟往來長江，停則依壘，行皆乘風，恆避戰，難得大創，乃謀襲燒之。

translations.literal: Yuebin reflected that rebel boats traveled the Yangtze, stopping to rely on fortifications when moored and sailing with the wind when moving, always avoiding battle and hard to inflict great damage; he therefore planned to raid and burn them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuebin saw rebel boats hugging shore forts when moored and running with the wind when moving, always avoiding decisive battle; he planned fire raids instead.

sentences.zh: 募壯士駕千石大船，實硝黃蘆荻，施火線。

translations.literal: He recruited brave men to man thousand-shi large boats, loaded with saltpeter, reeds, and rushes, fitted with fuse lines.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited volunteers for thousand-shi fire ships loaded with saltpeter, reeds, and rushes and fitted with fuses.

sentences.zh: 約曰：「近賊而發，急登舢板退。」

translations.literal: They agreed: "When close to rebels, ignite; then quickly board sampans and withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: The plan was: "Light the fuse near the enemy, then jump to sampans and withdraw."

sentences.zh: 應募者三百人，懸重賞。

translations.literal: Three hundred men answered the call; heavy rewards were posted.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred men volunteered for heavy rewards.

sentences.zh: 夜逼賊舟，於南岸嘴縱火，於是賊舟能​​戰者多燼。

translations.literal: By night they pressed close to rebel boats; at Nananzui they set fire; thus most rebel boats capable of fighting were burned.
translations.idiomatic: By night they closed on rebel boats and fired them at Nananzui, destroying most of the enemy's fighting fleet.

sentences.zh: 前軍直至黃州，旬日間轉戰數百里，擊毀賊舟六百餘，奪其資糧火藥，哨船掠巴河、蘄州、耀兵九江城下而還。

translations.literal: The vanguard reached Huangzhou; within ten days they fought over several hundred li, destroyed more than six hundred rebel boats, seized their supplies and gunpowder, scout boats raided Bahe and Qizhou, displayed force below Jiujiang city, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the vanguard fought several hundred li, destroyed more than six hundred boats, seized stores and powder, raided Bahe and Qizhou, showed force below Jiujiang, and returned.

sentences.zh: 武、漢水路援絕，乃益困。

translations.literal: Water routes to Wuchang and Hankou were cut off from relief and the rebels were thus more pressed.
translations.idiomatic: With river relief cut off, Wuchang and Hankou grew ever more desperate.

sentences.zh: 十一月，與李續賓陸師合攻。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he joined Li Xubin's land army in a joint attack.
translations.idiomatic: In November he joined Li Xubin's land forces in a combined assault.

sentences.zh: 值大風揚沙，波濤洶湧，水師上下環擊，賊大潰敗走。

translations.literal: A great wind raised sand; waves surged violently; the navy attacked above and below in encirclement; the rebels were routed and fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: A sand-laden gale whipped the river; the fleet struck from above and below; the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 二城同日克復，捷聞，加提督銜。

translations.literal: Both cities were recovered on the same day; when victory was reported, he was given the rank of commander.
translations.idiomatic: Both cities fell the same day; victory brought him the rank of commander.

sentences.zh: 進規九江，曾國籓以憂歸，薦岳斌接統其軍，彭玉麟副之。

translations.literal: Advancing on Jiujiang, Zeng Guofan returned home on account of mourning; he recommended Yuebin to take command of his army with Peng Yulin as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Jiujiang, Zeng Guofan went home in mourning and recommended Yuebin to succeed him with Peng Yulin as deputy.

sentences.zh: 分兵扼蘄州，破援賊。

translations.literal: He divided forces to block Qizhou and broke relieving rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He blocked Qizhou with detachments and routed relief columns.

sentences.zh: 秋，會陸軍克小池口，密與彭玉麟約期會攻湖口，克之。

translations.literal: In autumn the land army took Xiao-chikou; secretly he agreed with Peng Yulin on a date for joint attack on Hukou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn land forces took Xiao-chikou; he secretly timed a joint assault on Hukou with Peng Yulin and captured it.

sentences.zh: 於是內湖外江水師始復合。

translations.literal: Thereupon inner-lake and outer-river navies were reunited for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time the inner-lake and outer-river fleets were reunited.

sentences.zh: 乘勝奪小孤山，克彭澤，留軍屯之。

translations.literal: Seizing victory they took Xiaogushan and Pengze and left troops encamped there.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory they took Xiaogushan and Pengze and left garrisons behind.

sentences.zh: 自率前鋒至望江，賊望風遁，遂復東流。

translations.literal: He personally led the vanguard to Wangjiang; rebels fled at the sight of the wind and he recovered Dongliu.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the vanguard to Wangjiang he recovered Dongliu as rebels fled at his approach.

sentences.zh: 過安慶，攻樅陽、大通賊壘，克之。

translations.literal: Passing Anqing, he attacked fortifications at Zongyang and Datong and took them.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Anqing he stormed rebel forts at Zongyang and Datong and took them.

sentences.zh: 复銅陵，至蕪湖魯港，與江南師船會。

translations.literal: He recovered Tongling and reached Lugang at Wuhu, joining Jiangnan fleet boats.
translations.idiomatic: He retook Tongling, reached Lugang at Wuhu, and joined the Jiangnan fleet.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其轉戰千里，謀略過人，尋授福建陸路提督，許專摺奏事。

translations.literal: An edict praised his fighting over a thousand li and strategy surpassing others; soon he was appointed land commander of Fujian and permitted to report by memorial alone.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised his thousand-li campaign and superior strategy; soon he became land commander of Fujian with independent memorial rights.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，與李續賓會攻九江。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year he joined Li Xubin in attacking Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In April 1858 he and Li Xubin assaulted Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 岳斌當北門，臨江地雷發，奮呼齊登，擒賊首林啟榮，逸出之賊，盡為水師所殲，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Yuebin faced the north gate; a land mine exploded by the river; they shouted and climbed together; they captured the rebel chief Lin Qirong; fleeing rebels were all annihilated by the navy; he was granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Facing the north gate when a riverside mine blew, Yuebin's men stormed the walls, captured Lin Qirong, and the navy destroyed every fugitive; he received the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 詔促東下，疏言楚境肅清後始能會師，遂移屯黃石磯。

translations.literal: An edict urged eastward advance; he memorialized that only after the Chu region was pacified could armies unite; he then moved camp to Huangshiji.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered eastward he replied that armies could unite only after Hubei was cleared, and moved camp to Huangshiji.

sentences.zh: 連攻安慶、樅陽、大通，奪其壘，分兵復建德，調福建水師提督。

translations.literal: He repeatedly attacked Anqing, Zongyang, and Datong and took their fortifications; he divided forces to recover Jian'de and was transferred to commander of the Fujian navy.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly stormed Anqing, Zongyang, and Datong, retook Jian'de with detachments, and was transferred to commander of the Fujian navy.

sentences.zh: 九月，會都興阿克集賢關，賊自池州來援，迎擊於樅陽，破之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he joined Duxing'a at Jixian Pass; rebels from Chizhou came to relieve; he met and attacked them at Zongyang and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In September he joined Duxing'a at Jixian Pass, met Chizhou relief forces at Zongyang, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 時李續賓三河師潰，賊复謀上犯湖北。

translations.literal: At that time Li Xubin's army was routed at Sanhe; rebels again plotted to advance upstream against Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xubin's army was routed at Sanhe, rebels again plotted to drive upstream into Hubei.

sentences.zh: 岳斌遣兵分扼龍坪、鄔穴、田家鎮。

translations.literal: Yuebin sent troops to block Longping, Wuxue, and Tianjiazhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuebin dispatched detachments to hold Longping, Wuxue, and Tianjiazhen.

sentences.zh: 九年，督剿南北兩岸援賊，時出隊薄安慶城，以牽賊勢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he supervised suppression of relieving rebels on both north and south banks, at times sending columns to press close to Anqing city to divert rebel strength.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he hunted relief forces on both banks, sometimes skirmishing under Anqing's walls to pin enemy strength.

sentences.zh: 十二月，賊酋韋志俊以池州降，令攻蕪湖。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month rebel chief Wei Zhijun surrendered Chizhou and was ordered to attack Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: In December rebel chief Wei Zhijun surrendered Chizhou and was ordered to attack Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 其部下有叛者，還陷池州。

translations.literal: Among his subordinates were defectors who in turn seized Chizhou again.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his subordinates defected and retook Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 岳斌察志俊無異志，分別遣留，得精銳二千五百人，令率以助戰。

translations.literal: Yuebin saw that Zhijun had no disloyal intent, distinguished and kept or sent away men, obtained two thousand five hundred picked troops, and ordered him to lead them to assist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Zhijun still loyal, Yuebin sorted his men, kept two thousand five hundred picked troops under him, and sent them to battle.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成、李侍賢率眾分竄楚、皖，水師移屯觀音洲以備之。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng and Li Shixian led masses separately fleeing into Chu and Wan; the navy moved camp to Guanyinzhou to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng and Li Shixian scattered into Hubei and Anhui; the fleet shifted to Guanyinzhou to block them.
