sentences.zh: 十年四月，大破賊於蟂磯，令韋志俊拔殷家匯，進攻池州，毀城外石壘，潛襲樅陽，拔其城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year they routed rebels at Xiao-ji; he ordered Wei Zhijun to take Yinjiachui and advanced on Chizhou, destroyed outer stone fortifications, secretly raided Zongyang, and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: In April 1860 they routed rebels at Xiao-ji; Yuebin had Wei Zhijun take Yinjiachui, advanced on Chizhou, smashed outer stone forts, secretly raided Zongyang, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 秋，遣將攻池州，奪青溪關。

translations.literal: In autumn he sent generals to attack Chizhou and seized Qingxiguan.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he sent generals against Chizhou and seized Qingxiguan.

sentences.zh: 李秀成循江岸上竄，連敗之三山、光穴、子橋、白茅嘴、運漕鎮。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng fled up the riverbank and was repeatedly defeated at Sanshan, Guangxue, Ziqiao, Baimaozui, and Yuncao Town.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiucheng fled upriver and was repeatedly beaten at Sanshan, Guangxue, Ziqiao, Baimaozui, and Yuncao Town.

sentences.zh: 分兵入內湖，攻神廟山、鎮山，斷松林口浮橋。

translations.literal: He divided forces into the inner lake, attacked Shenmiaoshan and Zhenshan, and severed the floating bridge at Songlinkou.
translations.idiomatic: Detachments entered the inner lake, stormed Shenmiaoshan and Zhenshan, and cut the pontoon at Songlinkou.

sentences.zh: 冬，由魯港潛行百里，解南陵圍，拔出總兵陳大富一軍，及難民十餘萬，被珍賚。

translations.literal: In winter, traveling secretly a hundred li from Lugang, he relieved the siege of Nanling, extricated Major General Chen Dafu's entire army and more than one hundred thousand refugees, and was granted precious rewards.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he slipped a hundred li from Lugang, lifted the siege of Nanling, rescued Major General Chen Dafu's army and more than one hundred thousand refugees, and received imperial rewards.

sentences.zh: 十一年，合攻安慶，偕陸軍破赤岡嶺援賊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he joined in attacking Anqing and with the land army broke relieving rebels at Chigang Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he joined the siege of Anqing and with land forces broke relief columns at Chigang Ridge.

sentences.zh: 戰無為州神塘河，平其壘，焚賊船，劃菱湖兩岸賊屯。

translations.literal: At Shen-tang River in Wuwei Prefecture he leveled fortifications, burned rebel boats, and cleared rebel camps on both banks of Linghu.
translations.idiomatic: At Shen-tang River in Wuwei he leveled forts, burned boats, and cleared rebel camps along both banks of Linghu.

sentences.zh: 集攻安慶東門，乘勝拔城北諸壘，城賊窮蹙。

translations.literal: Gathering for attack on Anqing's east gate, they seized victory and took all fortifications north of the city; city rebels were driven to extremity.
translations.idiomatic: Massing on Anqing's east gate they swept the northern forts and drove the garrison to desperation.

sentences.zh: 八月，克安慶，遣總兵王明山、黃翼升克池州、桐城，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Anqing fell; he dispatched Major Generals Wang Mingshan and Huang Yisheng to take Chizhou and Tongcheng and granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
translations.idiomatic: Anqing fell in August; he sent Wang Mingshan and Huang Yisheng to take Chizhou and Tongcheng and received the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.

sentences.zh: 岳斌屢乞假省親，至是始歸。

translations.literal: Yuebin repeatedly asked leave to visit his parents; only then did he return home.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated requests for leave to visit his parents, Yuebin finally went home.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，以母病請展假，不允。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, on account of his mother's illness he asked to extend leave; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, with his mother ill, he asked to extend leave but was refused.

sentences.zh: 五月，至軍，移屯烏江。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he reached the army and moved camp to Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In May he rejoined the army and moved camp to Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 進攻金柱關，戰龍山橋，殲賊萬餘，

translations.literal: Advancing on Jinzhuguan, he fought at Longshan Bridge and annihilated more than ten thousand rebels,
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Jinzhuguan he fought at Longshan Bridge and destroyed more than ten thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊尋復來犯陣，斬賊酋陳緒賓，破護駕墩、石垝賊壘。

translations.literal: rebels soon came again to attack the formation; he beheaded the rebel chief Chen Xubin and broke fortifications at Hujiadun and Shigang.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels counterattacked he beheaded their chief Chen Xubin and stormed Hujiadun and Shigang.

sentences.zh: 自是江寧大營後路始固。

translations.literal: From then the rear of the great Jiangning camp was secure.
translations.idiomatic: From then the great Nanjing camp's rear was secure.

sentences.zh: 二年春，從曾國籓赴前敵大勝關、雨花台察視，與曾國荃定合圍之策。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he followed Zeng Guofan to the front to inspect Dasheng Pass and Yuhuatai and with Zeng Guoquan fixed the plan for combined encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1863 he followed Zeng Guofan to inspect Dasheng Pass and Yuhuatai and with Zeng Guoquan settled the encirclement plan.

sentences.zh: 三月，克黃池，悉收內河三里埂、伏龍橋、花津、護駕墩諸隘，以通寧國、蕪湖之路。

translations.literal: In the third month he took Huangchi and fully secured the inner-river passes Sanligeng, Fulong Bridge, Huajin, and Hujiadun to open the route to Ningguo and Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: In March he took Huangchi and secured Sanligeng, Fulong Bridge, Huajin, and Hujiadun, opening the route to Ningguo and Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 五月，克巢縣、含山、和州及江浦、浦口，破下關、草鞋峽、燕子磯，趨九洑洲，力戰拔之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he took Chaoxian, Hanshan, Hezhou, Jiangpu, and Pukou, broke Xiaguan, Caoxiexia, and Yanziji, pressed Jiufuzhou, and took it after fierce fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In May he retook Chaoxian, Hanshan, Hezhou, Jiangpu, and Pukou, broke Xiaguan, Caoxiexia, and Yanziji, and stormed Jiufuzhou after fierce fighting.

sentences.zh: 自是長江無賊舟。

translations.literal: From then there were no rebel boats on the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: After that no rebel boat remained on the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 十月，克高淳、寧國、建平、溧水，奪東壩要隘，江寧遂合圍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he took Gaochun, Ningguo, Jianping, and Lishui, seized the key pass at Dongba, and Jiangning was then fully encircled.
translations.idiomatic: In October he took Gaochun, Ningguo, Jianping, and Lishui, seized Dongba, and Nanjing was fully encircled.

sentences.zh: 岳斌因親病請歸養，詔賜其父母人葠四兩，慰留之。

translations.literal: Yuebin, on account of his parents' illness, asked to return home to care for them; an edict granted his parents four taels of ginseng each and comforted him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents fell ill Yuebin asked to go home; the throne sent each parent four taels of ginseng and urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 三年，命督辦江西、皖南軍務，援軍悉歸節制。

translations.literal: In the third year he was ordered to supervise military affairs in Jiangxi and southern Anhui; all relief armies were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he was ordered to supervise Jiangxi and southern Anhui; every relief army came under his command.

sentences.zh: 尋授陝甘總督，命俟江、皖賊氛淨儘後赴任。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu and ordered to take office only after Jiangsu-Anhui rebel disturbances were entirely cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu, to take office only after Jiangsu and Anhui were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 江寧平，加太子少保，予一等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was pacified he was given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the hereditary rank of First Class Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell he became Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the hereditary rank of First Class Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 六月，岳斌抵南昌，遣諸將克崇仁、東鄉、金谿、宜黃、南豐，解寧都圍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Yuebin reached Nanchang and dispatched generals to take Chongren, Dongxiang, Jinxi, Yihuang, and Nanfeng and lifted the siege of Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: In June Yuebin reached Nanchang, sent generals to take Chongren, Dongxiang, Jinxi, Yihuang, and Nanfeng, and lifted the siege of Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 秋，赴贛州，克瀘溪、新城、雩都，先後收降賊十餘萬，防境肅清。

translations.literal: In autumn he went to Ganzhou, took Luxi, Xincheng, and Yudu, and in succession received the surrender of more than one hundred thousand rebels; the defense region was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he took Luxi, Xincheng, and Yudu from Ganzhou and received more than one hundred thousand surrenders until the region was cleared.

sentences.zh: 复疏陳傷病親老，請開缺，不允，乃回籍募兵。

translations.literal: He again memorialized citing wounds, illness, and aged parents, asking to vacate his post; this was not granted; he then returned home to recruit troops.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to resign citing wounds, illness, and aged parents, was refused, and returned home to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 四年，率彭楚漢等新軍十營從行，抵西安。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he led Peng Chuhan and other new armies of ten battalions on the march and reached Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he marched to Xi'an with ten new battalions under Peng Chuhan and others.

sentences.zh: 會僧格林沁戰歿曹州，詔岳斌移兵入衛京畿。

translations.literal: When Sengge Rinchen died in battle at Caozhou, an edict ordered Yuebin to move troops to guard the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengge Rinchen fell at Caozhou, an edict ordered Yuebin to march and guard the capital region.

sentences.zh: 自請開缺，專任剿匪，不許，仍命速赴甘肅，六月，履任。

translations.literal: He himself asked to vacate his post and devote himself solely to suppressing bandits; this was not permitted; he was still ordered to hurry to Gansu; in the sixth month he assumed office.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to resign and fight bandits only; refused, he was ordered to hurry to Gansu and assumed office in June.

sentences.zh: 時甘回方熾，通省糜爛。

translations.literal: At that time Gansu Muslims were raging fiercely; the whole province was ravaged.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu Muslim rebels were then raging and the whole province lay in ruin.

sentences.zh: 雷正綰、曹克忠新敗於金積堡，都興阿、穆圖善攻寧夏未下，且奉命將出關；

translations.literal: Lei Zhengwan and Cao Kezhong had newly been defeated at Jinji Fort; Duxing'a and Mutushan attacked Ningxia without success and were also ordered to go beyond the pass;
translations.idiomatic: Lei Zhengwan and Cao Kezhong had just been beaten at Jinji Fort; Duxing'a and Mutushan failed before Ningxia and were ordered beyond the pass;

sentences.zh: 本省兵皆疲弱，疏調各省援兵，無一至者，僅自率新募之數千人；

translations.literal: provincial troops were all weak and worn; he memorialized calling for relief troops from every province, yet not one arrived; he had only the few thousand newly recruited men he personally led;
translations.idiomatic: provincial troops were exhausted; he called for aid from every province but none came, leading only a few thousand new recruits;

sentences.zh: 又因兵荒耕作久廢，饋運道塞，庫空如洗。

translations.literal: also because of war and famine cultivation had long been abandoned, supply routes were blocked, and the treasury was empty as if washed clean.
translations.idiomatic: war and famine had long stopped farming, supply routes were blocked, and the treasury was bare.

sentences.zh: 岳斌迭疏乞協餉，僅川、陝鄰省稍稍接濟，無以遍給。

translations.literal: Yuebin repeatedly memorialized begging coordinated pay; only neighboring Sichuan and Shaanxi gave slight assistance; there was no way to supply all.
translations.idiomatic: Yuebin repeatedly begged coordinated pay; only Sichuan and Shaanxi gave slight help, far short of need.

sentences.zh: 議進軍先搗靈州，繼規河、狄。

translations.literal: He planned to advance first against Lingzhou and then target He and Di.
translations.idiomatic: He planned first to strike Lingzhou, then Hezhou and Didao.

sentences.zh: 未幾，陶茂林、雷正綰兩軍相繼潰變。

translations.literal: Before long the armies of Tao Maolin and Lei Zhengwan in succession mutinied and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tao Maolin's and Lei Zhengwan's armies mutinied and collapsed in succession.

sentences.zh: 五年春，岳斌親赴涇州、慶陽視師。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year Yuebin personally went to Jingzhou and Qingyang to inspect the armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1866 Yuebin personally inspected armies at Jingzhou and Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 蘭州標兵遽變，圍署戕官，逼迫布政使林之望上疏，言糧餉獨厚楚軍，眾心不服。

translations.literal: Lanzhou garrison troops suddenly mutinied, besieged the yamen and killed officials, forcing Financial Commissioner Lin Zhiwang to memorialize that rations favored the Chu army alone and popular feeling was discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Lanzhou garrison troops mutinied, besieged the yamen, killed officials, and forced Financial Commissioner Lin Zhiwang to complain that rations favored Hunan troops.

sentences.zh: 岳斌聞警，先令曹克忠移師鎮撫，尋自回省城，按誅首犯百餘人，餘不問。

translations.literal: Yuebin, hearing the alarm, first ordered Cao Kezhong to move troops to pacify; soon he himself returned to the provincial capital, investigated and executed more than a hundred ringleaders, and did not question the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the alarm Yuebin sent Cao Kezhong to pacify the city, returned himself, executed more than a hundred ringleaders, and spared the rest.

sentences.zh: 以在途拆閱林之望奏摺，自請議處，革職留任，降三品頂戴。

translations.literal: Because on the road he opened and read Lin Zhiwang's memorial, he asked on his own initiative to be punished; he was dismissed from office but retained in post and demoted to third-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: For opening Lin Zhiwang's memorial en route he asked to be punished, was stripped of rank but kept in office, and demoted to third-grade insignia.

sentences.zh: 迭疏請罷，詔以左宗棠代之，未至，六年春，复陳病劇，乃命穆圖善暫署總督，許岳斌回籍。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized asking to be removed; an edict had Zuo Zongtang replace him; before Zuo arrived, in the spring of the sixth year he again memorialized that his illness was severe; then Mutushan was ordered temporarily to act as governor-general; Yuebin was permitted to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly asking to be removed, he was replaced by Zuo Zongtang; before Zuo arrived, in the spring of 1867 he reported grave illness, Mutushan acted temporarily, and Yuebin was allowed home.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，命偕彭玉麟巡閱長江，整頓水師，屢以親病請罷，五年，始允之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was ordered together with Peng Yulin to inspect the Yangtze and rectify the navy; he repeatedly asked to be dismissed on account of his parents' illness; in the fifth year this was finally granted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875 he was ordered with Peng Yulin to inspect the Yangtze navy, repeatedly asked leave for his parents' illness, and was finally released in 1879.

sentences.zh: 九年，法越戰事起，詔岳斌會辦福建軍務，未至，復命赴江南幫辦軍務。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Franco-Vietnamese war arose; an edict ordered Yuebin to assist in Fujian military affairs; before he arrived he was again ordered to assist military affairs in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1883 the Franco-Vietnamese war brought orders to assist in Fujian; before he arrived he was redirected to Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，率十二營赴援台灣，和議成，仍乞養歸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he led twelve battalions to aid Taiwan; when peace was concluded he again asked to retire and return home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1885 he led twelve battalions toward Taiwan; peace concluded, he again asked to retire home.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒於家，贈太子太保，照總督例賜卹，建專祠，諡勇愨。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died at home; he was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, condolence payments according to the precedent for a governor-general, a special shrine, and the posthumous name Yongque.
translations.idiomatic: In 1890 he died at home; the court made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted governor-general mourning, built a shrine, and gave the posthumous name Yongque, "Brave and Sincere."

sentences.zh: 岳斌與玉麟始終長江軍事，所部以功敘擢至提、鎮者不可勝數，實膺專閫者亦數十人。

translations.literal: Yuebin and Yulin from beginning to end handled Yangtze military affairs; subordinates promoted for merit to commander and major general were beyond counting; those who truly held independent command were also several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Yuebin and Yulin commanded Yangtze operations throughout; countless subordinates rose to commander and major general, and dozens held independent commands.

sentences.zh: =王明山=王明山，湘潭人。

translations.literal: Biography of Wang Mingshan. Wang Mingshan was a native of Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Wang Mingshan. Wang Mingshan came from Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 初隸岳斌營，積功至守備。

translations.literal: At first he served in Yuebin's battalion and through accumulated merit rose to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first served in Yang Yuebin's battalion and rose through merit to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 彭玉麟調領一營。

translations.literal: Peng Yulin transferred him to command one battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yulin transferred him to command a battalion.

sentences.zh: 戰鸚鵡洲，登陸破賊，攻金口先登，累擢游擊。

translations.literal: At Yingwuzhou he landed and broke rebels, at the assault on Jinkou was first to climb, and was repeatedly promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: At Yingwuzhou he landed and routed rebels; first over the wall at Jinkou, he rose repeatedly to colonel.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，補乾州協都司。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he was appointed battalion commander of the third rank in the Qianzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he was appointed battalion commander of the third rank in the Qianzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 攻漢陽，焚東南門賊船，連破賊於黃州樊口、富池口。

translations.literal: Attacking Hanyang he burned rebel boats at the southeast gate and repeatedly broke rebels at Fankou and Fuchikou at Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Assaulting Hanyang he burned boats at the southeast gate and repeatedly beat rebels at Fankou and Fuchikou near Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 戰武穴，伏蘆洲，伺賊登岸，突擊殲之。

translations.literal: At the battle of Wuxue he lay in ambush at Luzhou; waiting for rebels to land he suddenly attacked and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuxue he ambushed rebels at Luzhou and annihilated them as they landed.

sentences.zh: 回擊武昌援賊，累捷，擢參將。

translations.literal: Turning back he struck Wuchang relief rebels with repeated victories and was promoted to brigadier general.
translations.idiomatic: Wheeling back he repeatedly defeated Wuchang relief forces and was promoted brigadier general.

sentences.zh: 戰蘄州，焚賊舟七十餘。

translations.literal: At Qizhou he burned more than seventy rebel boats.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting at Qizhou, he put more than seventy rebel vessels to the torch.

sentences.zh: 登岸誘敵，賊聚攻，別隊乘虛襲城，克之，擢副將，賜號拔勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Landing to lure the enemy, when rebels massed to attack, another column seized the chance to raid the city and took it; he was promoted to vice commander and granted the title Bayong Batu.
translations.idiomatic: He landed as bait; when rebels massed against him another column seized the city; he was promoted vice commander and granted the title Bayong Batu.

sentences.zh: 進克黃州，會攻九江。

translations.literal: Advancing he took Huangzhou and joined the attack on Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to take Huangzhou and joined the siege of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 八年，授浙江金華協副將。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed vice commander of the Jinhua garrison in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he was appointed vice commander of the Jinhua garrison in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 克東流，薄安慶，毀城外賊壘，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: He took Dongliu, pressed close to Anqing, destroyed outer rebel fortifications, and was registered for appointment as major general.
translations.idiomatic: He took Dongliu, closed on Anqing, destroyed outer forts, and was marked for major general.

sentences.zh: 九年，乞假回籍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he asked leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he asked leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 會石達開犯湖南，率隊自衡州趨祁陽要擊之，破賊於毛家埠。

translations.literal: When Shi Dakai invaded Hunan he led a column from Hengzhou to intercept at Qiyang and broke rebels at Maojiapu.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai invaded Hunan he marched from Hengzhou to intercept at Qiyang and routed rebels at Maojiapu.

sentences.zh: 十年，授安徽壽春鎮總兵，破賊蕪湖蟂磯、義橋。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed major general of the Shouchun garrison in Anhui and broke rebels at Xiao-ji and Yiqiao at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he became major general of Shouchun garrison and beat rebels at Xiao-ji and Yiqiao near Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 十一年，破賊練潭鎮，斬其渠龔天福。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he broke rebels at Liantan Town and beheaded their leader Gong Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he broke rebels at Liantan Town and beheaded their leader Gong Tianfu.

sentences.zh: 復會陸師克赤岡嶺，遂下安慶。

translations.literal: He again joined the land army in taking Chigang Ridge and then took Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined land forces at Chigang Ridge and then helped take Anqing.

sentences.zh: 楊岳斌假歸，令明山代統其軍。

translations.literal: When Yang Yuebin went home on leave he ordered Mingshan to take temporary command of his army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yuebin went on leave he left Mingshan in temporary command.

sentences.zh: 連复池州、銅陵、破泥汊口、神塘河諸壘。

translations.literal: He repeatedly recovered Chizhou and Tongling and broke fortifications at Nizhakou and Shen-tang River.
translations.idiomatic: He retook Chizhou and Tongling and broke forts at Nizhakou and Shen-tang River.

sentences.zh: 克無為州，別遣將遏巢湖口，克運漕鎮，進拔東關。

translations.literal: He took Wuwei Prefecture, separately sent generals to block Chaohu mouth, took Yuncao Town, and advanced to take Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: He took Wuwei Prefecture, blocked Chaohu mouth, captured Yuncao Town, and advanced to Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢福建陸路提督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted to land commander of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was promoted land commander of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 克銅城徬，復和州、含山、巢縣，殲逸賊於木橋、沙洲，又破之江心洲、西梁山。

translations.literal: He took Tongcheng Pass, recovered Hezhou, Hanshan, and Chaoxian, annihilated fleeing rebels at Muqiao and Shazhou, and again broke them at Jiangxinzhou and Xiliangshan.
translations.idiomatic: He took Tongcheng Pass, retook Hezhou, Hanshan, and Chaoxian, destroyed fugitives at Muqiao and Shazhou, and beat them again at Jiangxinzhou and Xiliangshan.

sentences.zh: 尋以傷病乞假歸。

translations.literal: Soon he asked leave to return home on account of wounds and illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon wounds and illness drove him to ask leave and go home.

sentences.zh: 明山在軍十餘年，屢當大敵。

translations.literal: Mingshan was in the army more than ten years and repeatedly faced great enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan served more than ten years in the field and repeatedly faced major enemy forces.

sentences.zh: 江南平，遂不出。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified he did not go out again.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangnan was pacified he never returned to active service.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，圖功臣像於紫光閣，明山與焉。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu reign portraits of meritorious ministers were painted in the Hall of Purple Glories; Mingshan was among them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu reign his portrait joined those of meritorious ministers in the Hall of Purple Glories.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒於家，賜血卩。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died at home and was granted blood-money condolence payments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1890 he died at home and received blood-money condolence payments.

sentences.zh: =孫昌凱=孫昌凱，清泉人。

translations.literal: Biography of Sun Changkai. Sun Changkai was a native of Qingquan.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Sun Changkai. Sun Changkai came from Qingquan.

sentences.zh: 入水師，積功擢千總。

translations.literal: He entered the navy and through accumulated merit was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the river fleet and rose through merit to company commander.

sentences.zh: 昌凱舊業鐵工，田家鎮之戰，領小舟為頭隊。

translations.literal: Changkai's former trade was ironworking; at the battle of Tianjiazhen he led small boats as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: A blacksmith by trade, Changkai led the vanguard of small boats at Tianjiazhen.

sentences.zh: 冒槍砲鼓備斷鐵​​鎖，纜開，大呼猛進，筏上賊潰走。

translations.literal: Braving musket fire he beat drums and prepared tools to sever the iron chains; the cables opened; he shouted and charged forward; rebels on the rafts fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Under musket fire he worked with maul and axe to cut the iron chains; as the barrier opened he shouted and drove forward and rebels on the rafts fled.

sentences.zh: 後隊縱火，賊舟盡焚。

translations.literal: The rear squadrons set fire and all rebel boats were burned.
translations.idiomatic: Rear squadrons set the fire that burned every rebel boat.

sentences.zh: 功最，擢守備。

translations.literal: For foremost merit he was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: For the foremost merit he was promoted battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，破賊漢口，擢都司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng he broke rebels at Hankou and was promoted to battalion commander of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he routed rebels at Hankou and was promoted battalion commander of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 六年，從攻武昌，焚賊舟，授廣東陸路提標游擊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he joined the attack on Wuchang, burned rebel boats, and was appointed colonel in the Guangdong land commander's garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he joined the assault on Wuchang, burned rebel boats, and was appointed colonel in the Guangdong land commander's garrison.

sentences.zh: 七年，從平蘄、黃賊巢，克小池口、湖口，擢參將。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed in pacifying Qizhou and Huangzhou rebel nests, took Xiao-chikou and Hukou, and was promoted to brigadier general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he helped pacify Qizhou and Huangzhou, took Xiao-chikou and Hukou, and was promoted brigadier general.

sentences.zh: 克九江，加副將銜，補兩廣督標參將。

translations.literal: When Jiujiang was taken he was given vice commander's rank and appointed brigadier general in the Two Guang commander's garrison.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall of Jiujiang he received vice commander's rank and a brigadier's post in the Two Guang commander's garrison.

sentences.zh: 九年，回援湖南，防祁陽、衡州，擢惠州協副將。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he returned to relieve Hunan, defended Qiyang and Hengzhou, and was promoted vice commander of the Huizhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he returned to relieve Hunan, defended Qiyang and Hengzhou, and was promoted vice commander of the Huizhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 以母病乞養開缺。

translations.literal: On account of his mother's illness he asked to retire and vacate his post.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill he asked to retire and vacate his post.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，彭玉麟疏薦昌凱誠實篤毅，驍果善戰，授浙江海門鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu reign Peng Yulin memorialized recommending Changkai as honest, steadfast, and resolute, brave and skilled in battle, and appointed him major general of the Haimen garrison in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangxu, Peng Yulin recommended Changkai as honest, resolute, and valiant in battle and had him appointed major general of Haimen garrison in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，改署任，留襄海防。

translations.literal: When mourning for his mother ended he changed to acting appointment and remained to assist coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning he served in acting appointment on coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 事定，請終制。

translations.literal: When matters were settled he asked to complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs settled he asked to complete mourning properly.

sentences.zh: 後仍補原官，調署處州鎮。

translations.literal: Later he still filled his original post and was transferred to act as commander of the Chuzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Later he resumed his original post and was transferred to act as commander of the Chuzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，卒，賜卹，附祀彭玉麟祠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he died; condolence payments were granted and he was attached in sacrifice at Peng Yulin's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In 1895 he died; mourning payments were granted and he was enshrined with Peng Yulin.

sentences.zh: =楊明海=楊明海，長沙人。

translations.literal: Biography of Yang Minghai. Yang Minghai was a native of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Yang Minghai. Yang Minghai came from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 入水師，洊擢守備。

translations.literal: He entered the navy and was repeatedly promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the river fleet and rose repeatedly to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，戰樅陽、殷家匯、池州、蟂磯，迭破賊，擢都司。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he fought at Zongyang, Yinjiachui, Chizhou, and Xiao-ji, repeatedly broke rebels, and was promoted to battalion commander of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he fought at Zongyang, Yinjiachui, Chizhou, and Xiao-ji, beat rebels repeatedly, and was promoted battalion commander of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 十一年，克南陵，擢游擊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he took Nanling and was promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he took Nanling and was promoted colonel.

sentences.zh: 克安慶，擢副將。

translations.literal: When Anqing was taken he was promoted to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall of Anqing he was promoted vice commander.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從攻東梁山、金柱關，裹創血戰，功最，以總兵記名，賜號忱勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he joined the attack on Dongliangshan and Jinzhuguan, fought wrapped in wounds and bloody battle with foremost merit, was registered for appointment as major general, and granted the title Chenyong Batu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he fought wounded at Dongliangshan and Jinzhuguan with foremost merit, was marked for major general, and granted the title Chenyong Batu.

sentences.zh: 二年，大捷於九洑洲，以提督記名。

translations.literal: In the second year he won a great victory at Jiufuzhou and was registered for appointment as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he won a great victory at Jiufuzhou and was marked for commander.

sentences.zh: 戰江寧小沙口，先登陷陣，砲子穿右股，率哨船渡江，從陸軍進剿蘇州，授山東兗州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: At Xiaoshakou in Jiangning he was first to climb and plunge into battle; a cannon ball pierced his right thigh; he led scout boats across the river and followed the land army in suppressing Suzhou; he was appointed major general of the Yanzhou garrison in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanjing's Xiaoshakou he led the escalade; a round shot pierced his right thigh; he still ferried scout boats across the river and followed land forces against Suzhou; he was appointed major general of Yanzhou garrison in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 蘇州复，遂留防。

translations.literal: When Suzhou was recovered he remained on garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: After Suzhou was retaken he remained on garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 三年，楊岳斌赴甘肅，調明海偕彭楚漢率所募兵從行，破回匪於金縣夏官營，晉號格洪額巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Yang Yuebin went to Gansu, Minghai was transferred with Peng Chuhan to lead recruited troops on the march; they broke Muslim rebels at Xiaguanying in Jinxian and he was advanced to the title Gehong'e Batu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864, when Yang Yuebin went to Gansu, Minghai marched with Peng Chuhan, routed Muslim rebels at Xiaguanying in Jinxian, and received the title Gehong'e Batu.

sentences.zh: 軍食久乏，明海奉檄治糧運。

translations.literal: Army provisions had long been scarce; Minghai received orders to manage grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: With army rations long exhausted, Minghai was ordered to manage grain transport.

sentences.zh: 八年，赴兗州鎮本任。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he went to his substantive post at the Yanzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 he took up his substantive post at Yanzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，母憂去官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875 he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 七年，授狼山鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed major general of the Langshan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 he was appointed major general of Langshan garrison.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒，賜卹。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died; condolence payments were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1885 he died and mourning payments were granted.

sentences.zh: =謝濬畬=謝濬畬，原名得勝，長沙人。

translations.literal: Biography of Xie Junshe. Xie Junshe, original name Desheng, was a native of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Xie Junshe. Xie Junshe, originally named Desheng, came from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 充水師哨長，進攻武昌，濬畬自請為前鋒。

translations.literal: Serving as a navy outpost chief, in the advance on Wuchang Junshe volunteered to be vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: As a navy outpost chief he volunteered for the vanguard in the advance on Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 突鹽關賊壘，薄鸚鸝洲，與陸師夾擊，克武、漢，戰蘄州田家鎮，累功擢守備。

translations.literal: He suddenly struck the rebel fort at Yanguan, pressed close to Yingwuzhou, and with the land army attacked from both sides; Wuchang and Hankou were taken; at Qizhou and Tianjiazhen he repeatedly earned merit and was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed the Yanguan rebel fort, closed on Yingwuzhou, coordinated with land forces to retake Wuchang and Hankou, and at Qizhou and Tianjiazhen earned repeated promotion to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 克九江，擢都司。

translations.literal: When Jiujiang was taken he was promoted to battalion commander of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall of Jiujiang he was promoted battalion commander of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 破賊赤岡嶺，擢游擊。

translations.literal: Breaking rebels at Chigang Ridge he was promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: At Chigang Ridge he routed rebels and was promoted colonel.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從彭玉麟克太平及金柱關、東梁山、秣陵關、九洑洲諸要隘，擢副將。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Peng Yulin in taking Taiping and the key passes Jinzhuguan, Dongliangshan, Moling Pass, and Jiufuzhou and was promoted to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he followed Peng Yulin in taking Taiping, Jinzhuguan, Dongliangshan, Moling Pass, and Jiufuzhou and was promoted vice commander.

sentences.zh: 江寧平，以總兵記名，授提標中軍副將。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was pacified he was registered for appointment as major general and appointed vice commander of the commander's central army.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell he was marked for major general and appointed vice commander of the commander's central army.

sentences.zh: 光緒十八年，擢瓜洲鎮總兵，兼署水師提督，調署漢陽鎮。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Guangxu he was promoted major general of the Guazhou garrison, also acting commander of the navy, and transferred to act as commander of the Hanyang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1892 he became major general of Guazhou garrison, also acting navy commander, and was transferred to act as commander of the Hanyang garrison.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，卒於官，賜卹，附祀彭玉麟祠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died in office; condolence payments were granted and he was attached in sacrifice at Peng Yulin's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In 1901 he died in office; mourning payments were granted and he was enshrined with Peng Yulin.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：彭玉麟、楊岳斌佐曾國籓創立水師，為滅賊根本。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Peng Yulin and Yang Yuebin assisted Zeng Guofan in founding the navy, which was fundamental to destroying the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say Peng Yulin and Yang Yuebin helped Zeng Guofan found the river fleet—the foundation of rebel destruction.

sentences.zh: 兩人勳績，頡頏相並。

translations.literal: The two men's achievements matched each other in eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Their achievements stood equal in eminence.

sentences.zh: 岳斌後為朝旨強促西征，用違其才，僨事損望。

translations.literal: Yuebin afterward was strongly pressed by court orders to campaign westward; use went against his talent and failure damaged expectations.
translations.idiomatic: Yuebin was later forced west by court orders; the wrong assignment wasted his talent and damaged his reputation.

sentences.zh: 玉麟終身不任官職，巡閱長江，為國家紓東顧之憂。

translations.literal: Yulin all his life did not hold office; inspecting the Yangtze he relieved the state's worry over the east.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin never held regular office; inspecting the Yangtze he eased the dynasty's eastern worries.

sentences.zh: 其疏論古人晚節之失，由於不能自藏其短，且惜朝廷不善全其長，洵至言也。

translations.literal: His memorial discussing the late-years failures of men of old, because they could not hide their own shortcomings, and also regretting that the court did not know how well to preserve their strengths, was truly words to the point.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial on how great men fall in old age by failing to hide their flaws—and how courts fail to preserve their strengths—was profoundly true.

sentences.zh: 後盛昱劾其辭尚書之命，乃謂抗詔鳴高，殆淺之乎測玉麟矣。

translations.literal: Later Sheng Yu impeached his declining the minister's appointment, saying he defied the edict and affected loftiness; that was perhaps too shallow a measure of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sheng Yu impeached him for refusing the ministry as edict-defying posturing—a shallow reading of Peng Yulin indeed.
